bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =【晉紀十八】=

translations.literal: Jin Annals 18
translations.idiomatic: Jin Annals 18

sentences.zh: 起著雍淹茂，盡重光赤奮若，凡四年。

translations.literal: From Zhuoyong Yanmao through Chongguang Chifenruo; four years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhuoyong Yanmao through Chongguang Chifenruo—four years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕王皝遣都尉趙槃如趙，聽師期。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, King Murong Huang of Yan sent Commandant Zhao Pan to Zhao to coordinate the timing of the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the King of Yan, Murong Huang, sent Commandant Zhao Pan to Zhao to arrange the schedule for the joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎將擊段遼，募驍勇者三萬人，悉拜龍騰中郎。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao was about to attack Duan Liao; he recruited thirty thousand fierce warriors and all appointed them Dragon Soaring Central Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao was preparing to attack Duan Liao. He recruited thirty thousand bold fighters and appointed them all Dragon Soaring Central Commandants.

sentences.zh: 會遼遣段屈雲襲趙幽州，幽州刺史李孟退保易京。

translations.literal: Just then Liao sent Duan Quyun to raid Zhao's You Province; You Governor Li Meng withdrew to defend Yijing.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Duan Liao sent Duan Quyun to strike Zhao's You Province, and Governor Li Meng of You fell back to hold Yijing.

sentences.zh: 虎乃以桃豹為橫海將軍，王華為渡遼將軍，帥舟師十萬出漂渝津；

translations.literal: Hu then made Tao Bao Crossing-the-Seas General and Wang Hua Crossing-Liao General, leading a fleet of one hundred thousand out from Piaoyu Ford;
translations.idiomatic: Hu then appointed Tao Bao Crossing-the-Seas General and Wang Hua Crossing-Liao General, and led a fleet of one hundred thousand men out from Piaoyu Ford;

sentences.zh: 支雄為龍驤大將軍，姚弋仲為冠軍將軍，帥步騎七萬前鋒以伐遼。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiong as Dragon Prancing Grand General and Yao Yizhong as Champion General, leading seventy thousand infantry and cavalry as the vanguard to attack Liao.
translations.idiomatic: with Zhi Xiong as Dragon Prancing Grand General and Yao Yizhong as Champion General leading seventy thousand foot and horse as the vanguard against Liao.

sentences.zh: 三月，趙槃還至棘城。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhao Pan returned to Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhao Pan returned to Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝引兵攻掠令支以北諸城。

translations.literal: King Murong Huang of Yan led troops to attack and plunder the cities north of Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang of Yan then led his army to raid the cities north of Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 段遼將追之。

translations.literal: Duan Liao was about to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao prepared to give chase.

sentences.zh: 慕容翰曰：「今趙兵在南，當並力御之；

translations.literal: Murong Han said, "Now the Zhao army is in the south; we ought to unite our strength to resist them;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han said, "The Zhao forces are in the south now—we should combine our strength to hold them off;

sentences.zh: 而更與燕鬥，燕王自將而來，其士卒精銳，若萬一失利，將何以御南敵乎！」

translations.literal: yet instead we fight Yan. The Yan king comes in person; his soldiers are keen and elite. If by any chance we lose, how will we resist the southern enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: yet you would turn to fight Yan. The Yan king leads the army himself, and his troops are sharp and seasoned. If we should lose, how will we face the enemy in the south?"

sentences.zh: 段蘭怒曰：「吾前為卿所誤，以成今日之患，吾不復墮卿計中矣！」

translations.literal: Duan Lan angrily said, "I was misled by you before, which brought on today's disaster. I will not fall into your schemes again!"
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lan burst out, "You misled me once before and brought on this disaster. I will not be taken in by your counsel again!"

sentences.zh: 乃悉將見眾追之。

translations.literal: He then led all the troops he had at hand in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out with every man he had to pursue the Yan army.

sentences.zh: 皝設伏以待之，大破蘭兵，斬首數千級，掠五千戶及畜產萬計以歸。

translations.literal: Huang set an ambush to await them, routed Lan's army utterly, took several thousand heads, and returned with five thousand households and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Huang laid an ambush and crushed Lan's force, taking several thousand heads and returning with five thousand households and vast herds of livestock.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎進屯金台。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao advanced and encamped at Jintai.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao advanced and encamped at Jintai.

sentences.zh: 支雄長驅入薊，段遼所署漁陽、上谷、代郡守相皆降，取四十餘城。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiong drove straight into Ji; the prefects and chancellors of Yuyang, Shanggu, and Dai that Duan Liao had appointed all surrendered, and more than forty cities were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xiong swept into Ji. The officials Duan Liao had placed over Yuyang, Shanggu, and Dai all submitted, and more than forty cities fell to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 北平相陽裕帥其民數千家登燕山以自固，諸將恐其為後患，欲攻之。

translations.literal: Beiping Chancellor Yang Yu led several thousand of his people up Mount Yan to fortify themselves; the generals feared he would become a threat in the rear and wished to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu, chancellor of Beiping, led several thousand of his people onto Mount Yan to hold out. The generals feared a threat to their rear and wanted to attack him.

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「裕儒生，矜惜名節，恥於迎降耳，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Hu said, "Yu is a Confucian scholar who cherishes his reputation and is ashamed to come out and surrender; he can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Yu is a scholar who prizes his name and is too ashamed to come out and surrender. He cannot harm us."

sentences.zh: 遂過之，至徐無。

translations.literal: He then passed by and reached Xuwu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed on and reached Xuwu.

sentences.zh: 段遼以弟蘭既敗，不必復戰，帥妻子、宗族、豪大千餘家，棄令支，奔密雲山。

translations.literal: Duan Liao, seeing his brother Lan already defeated, felt there was no need to fight again; he led his wife and children, clan, and more than a thousand great households, abandoned Lingzhi, and fled to Miyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his brother Lan already beaten, Duan Liao saw no point in fighting on. He took his family, his clan, and more than a thousand leading households, abandoned Lingzhi, and fled to Miyun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 將行，執慕容翰手泣曰：「不用卿言，自取敗亡。

translations.literal: As he was about to leave, he took Murong Han's hand and wept, saying, "I did not heed your words and brought defeat on myself.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, he seized Murong Han's hand and wept. "I would not listen to you and brought this ruin on myself.

sentences.zh: 我固苦心，令卿失所，深以為愧。」

translations.literal: My heart has long been troubled, and I have caused you to lose your place; I am deeply ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: My heart has long been heavy, and I have left you without a home. I am deeply ashamed."

sentences.zh: 翰北奔宇文氏。

translations.literal: Han fled north to the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Han fled north to the Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 遼左右長史劉群、盧諶、崔悅等封府庫請降。

translations.literal: Liao's Left and Right Chief Administrators Liu Qun, Lu Chen, Cui Yue, and others sealed the treasury and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's chief administrators Liu Qun, Lu Chen, Cui Yue, and others sealed the treasury and offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 虎遣將軍郭太、麻秋帥輕騎二萬追遼，至密雲山。

translations.literal: Hu sent Generals Guo Tai and Ma Qiu with twenty thousand light cavalry in pursuit of Liao, reaching Miyun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Generals Guo Tai and Ma Qiu with twenty thousand light horse in pursuit, as far as Miyun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 獲其母妻，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: They captured his mother and wife and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: They seized his mother and wife and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 遼單騎走險，遣其子乞特真奉表及獻名馬於趙，虎受之。

translations.literal: Liao fled alone through difficult terrain; he sent his son Qitezhen to present a memorial and offer famous horses to Zhao, and Hu accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liao fled alone through the mountains. He sent his son Qitezhen with a petition and famous horses to Zhao, and Hu accepted his submission.

sentences.zh: 虎入令支官，論功封賞各有差。

translations.literal: Hu entered the Lingzhi government offices and rewarded merit with enfeoffments and gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hu entered the government halls at Lingzhi and distributed rewards according to each man's merit.

sentences.zh: 徙段國民二萬餘戶於司、雍、兗、豫四州；

translations.literal: He relocated more than twenty thousand households of the Duan people to the four provinces of Si, Yong, Yan, and Yu;
translations.idiomatic: He moved more than twenty thousand Duan households to Si, Yong, Yan, and Yu;

sentences.zh: 士大夫之有才行，皆擢敘之。

translations.literal: scholars and officials of talent and conduct were all promoted and registered.
translations.idiomatic: and every capable scholar-official was given office and rank.

sentences.zh: 陽裕詣軍門降。

translations.literal: Yang Yu came to the camp gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yu came to the camp gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 虎讓之曰：「卿昔為奴虜走，今為士人來，豈識知天命，將逃匿無地邪？」

translations.literal: Hu reproached him, saying, "You once fled as a captive slave; now you come as a gentleman. Do you recognize Heaven's mandate, or will you have nowhere left to hide?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu rebuked him: "You once fled as a captive. Now you come as a gentleman. Do you finally see Heaven's mandate, or do you think you still have somewhere to hide?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣昔事王公，不能匡濟；

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant once served the royal lord but could not set things right;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I once served a royal lord and could not save him;

sentences.zh: 逃於段氏，復不能全。

translations.literal: I fled to the Duan clan but again could not preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: I fled to the Duan and again could not preserve them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下天網高張，籠絡四海，幽、冀豪傑莫不風從，如臣比肩，無所獨愧。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's net of Heaven is spread wide, gathering all within the four seas; the heroes of You and Ji all follow like the wind. Men like me are countless—there is nothing for which I alone should feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's net covers the realm, and the heroes of You and Ji answer your call. I am only one among many—there is no special shame in my coming.

sentences.zh: 生死之命，惟陛下制之！」

translations.literal: Whether I live or die is for Your Majesty alone to decide!"
translations.idiomatic: Life and death are in Your Majesty's hands alone!"

sentences.zh: 虎悅，即拜北平太守。

translations.literal: Hu was pleased and immediately appointed him Chancellor of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was pleased and at once appointed him Chancellor of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸丑，以慕容皝為征北大將軍、幽州牧，領平州刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, Murong Huang was made Pacification-of-the-North Grand General, Governor of You, and concurrently Governor of Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guichou, Murong Huang was appointed Pacification-of-the-North Grand General, Governor of You, and concurrently Governor of Ping.

sentences.zh: 成主期驕虐日甚，多所誅殺，而籍沒其資財、婦女，由是大臣多不自安。

translations.literal: Lord of Cheng Qi grew daily more arrogant and cruel, executing many and confiscating their property and women; because of this, many ministers no longer felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Qi of Cheng grew more arrogant and cruel by the day. He executed many men and seized their goods and women, and the great ministers grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 漢王壽素貴重，有威名，期及建寧王越等皆忌之。

translations.literal: King of Han Shou had long been honored and held authority and a formidable reputation; Qi and Prince of Jianning Yue and others all envied and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: King Shou of Han had long been eminent and commanded respect. Qi, Prince Yue of Jianning, and others all resented and feared him.

sentences.zh: 壽懼不免，每當入朝，常詐為邊書，辭以警急。

translations.literal: Shou feared he could not escape harm; whenever he was to attend court, he would feign frontier dispatches and plead urgent alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Shou feared for his life. Whenever he was summoned to court, he forged frontier reports and pleaded urgent border alarms.

sentences.zh: 初，巴西處士龔壯，父、叔皆為李特所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, the reclusive gentleman of Baxi, Gong Zhuang, had both his father and uncle killed by Li Te.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was Gong Zhuang, a recluse of Baxi, whose father and uncle had both been killed by Li Te.

sentences.zh: 壯欲報仇，積年不除喪。

translations.literal: Zhuang wished to avenge them and for years did not lay aside mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang sought revenge and for years refused to end his mourning.

sentences.zh: 壽數以禮辟之，壯不應；

translations.literal: Shou repeatedly summoned him by proper ritual, but Zhuang did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: Shou repeatedly invited him by proper ceremony, but Zhuang would not answer;

sentences.zh: 而往見壽，壽密問壯以自安之策。

translations.literal: yet Zhuang went to see Shou, and Shou privately asked Zhuang for a plan to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: yet Zhuang came to see Shou, and Shou privately asked him how he might save himself.

sentences.zh: 壯曰：「巴、蜀之民本皆晉臣，節下若能發兵西取成都，稱籓於晉，誰不爭為節下奮臂前驅者？

translations.literal: Zhuang said, "The people of Ba and Shu were originally all subjects of Jin. If my lord can raise troops and march west to take Chengdu and declare yourself a vassal of Jin, who would not strive to lead the way for you?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang said, "The people of Ba and Shu were Jin subjects at heart. If you march west and take Chengdu, then declare yourself a vassal of Jin, who would not rush to fight at your side?

sentences.zh: 如此則福流子孫，名垂不朽，豈徒脫今日之禍而已！」

translations.literal: Thus blessings would flow to your descendants and your name would endure undying—how could it be only to escape today's peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Your line would prosper and your name would live forever—not merely escape today's danger!"

sentences.zh: 壽然之，陰與長史略陽羅恆、巴西解思明謀攻成都。

translations.literal: Shou agreed; in secret he plotted with Chief Administrator of Lueyang Luo Heng and Administrator of Baxi Xie Siming to attack Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shou agreed. In secret he plotted with his chief administrator Luo Heng of Lueyang and Xie Siming of Baxi to seize Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 期頗聞之，數遣許涪至壽所，伺其動靜；

translations.literal: Qi had heard something of this and repeatedly sent Xu Fu to Shou's headquarters to watch his movements;
translations.idiomatic: Qi had caught wind of this and sent Xu Fu again and again to Shou's camp to watch him;

sentences.zh: 又鴆殺壽養弟安北將軍攸。

translations.literal: and also poisoned Shou's foster brother, Pacification-of-the-North General You.
translations.idiomatic: and he poisoned Shou's foster brother You, Pacification-of-the-North General.

sentences.zh: 壽乃詐為妹夫任調書，雲期當取壽；

translations.literal: Shou then forged a letter in the name of his brother-in-law Ren Diao, saying Qi was about to seize Shou;
translations.idiomatic: Shou forged a letter in the name of his brother-in-law Ren Diao, claiming that Qi was about to arrest him;

sentences.zh: 其眾信之，遂帥步騎萬餘人自涪襲成都，許賞以城中財物，以其將李弈為前鋒。

translations.literal: his troops believed it, and he led more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Fu in a surprise attack on Chengdu, promising the city's goods as reward and making his general Li Yi the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: his men believed him, and he led more than ten thousand foot and horse from Fu in a surprise march on Chengdu, promising the city's wealth as booty and putting Li Yi at the head.

sentences.zh: 期不意其至，初不設備。

translations.literal: Qi did not expect his arrival and at first made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Qi never expected him and had made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 壽世子勢為翊軍校尉，開門納之，遂克成都，屯兵宮門。

translations.literal: Shou's heir Shi was Assistant Commander of the Support Army; he opened the gates and admitted them, and they took Chengdu and encamped at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's heir Shi, Assistant Commander of the Support Army, opened the gates to them. They took Chengdu and encamped at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 期遣侍中勞壽。

translations.literal: Qi sent a Palace Attendant to console Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent a Palace Attendant to greet Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽奏建寧王越、景騫、田褒、姚華、許涪及征西將軍李遐、將軍李西等懷奸亂政，皆收殺之。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized that Prince of Jianning Yue, Jing Qian, Tian Bao, Yao Hua, Xu Fu, and Western Campaign General Li Xia, General Li Xi, and others harbored treachery and disturbed government; all were arrested and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shou reported that Prince Yue of Jianning, Jing Qian, Tian Bao, Yao Hua, Xu Fu, Western Campaign General Li Xia, General Li Xi, and others had plotted treason. All were seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 縱兵大掠，數日乃定。

translations.literal: He let the troops plunder freely; only after several days did order return.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers looted the city for days before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 壽矯以太后任氏令廢期為邛都縣公，幽之別宮。

translations.literal: Shou forged an order in the name of Empress Dowager Ren to depose Qi as Duke of Qiongdu and confine him in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shou forged an order from Empress Dowager Ren deposing Qi as Duke of Qiongdu and confining him in a separate palace.

sentences.zh: 追謚戾太子曰哀皇帝。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored the Deposed Crown Prince with the title Emperor Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored the Deposed Crown Prince as Emperor Ai.

sentences.zh: 羅恆、解思明、李弈等勸壽稱鎮西將軍、益州牧、成都王，稱籓於晉，送邛都公於建康；

translations.literal: Luo Heng, Xie Siming, Li Yi, and others urged Shou to take the title Western Campaign General, Governor of Yi, and King of Chengdu, declare himself a vassal of Jin, and send the Duke of Qiongdu to Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: Luo Heng, Xie Siming, Li Yi, and others urged Shou to take the titles Western Campaign General, Governor of Yi, and King of Chengdu, submit to Jin as a vassal, and send the Duke of Qiongdu to Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 任調及司馬蔡興、侍中李艷等勸壽自稱帝。

translations.literal: Ren Diao and Chief Clerk Cai Xing, Palace Attendant Li Yan, and others urged Shou to declare himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Diao, Chief Clerk Cai Xing, Palace Attendant Li Yan, and others urged him to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 壽命筮之，占者曰：「可數年天子。」

translations.literal: Shou ordered divination; the diviner said, "You may be Son of Heaven for several years."
translations.idiomatic: Shou had the matter divined. The diviner said, "You may reign as Son of Heaven for several years."

sentences.zh: 調喜曰：「一日尚足，況數年乎！」

translations.literal: Diao rejoiced and said, "Even one day would be enough—how much more several years!"
translations.idiomatic: Diao exclaimed with delight, "One day would be enough—how much more several years!"

sentences.zh: 思明曰：「數年天子，孰與百世諸侯？」

translations.literal: Siming said, "Several years as Son of Heaven—how does that compare with being a feudal lord for a hundred generations?"
translations.idiomatic: Siming said, "A few years as emperor—how does that compare with being a feudal lord for a hundred generations?"

sentences.zh: 壽曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。」

translations.literal: Shou said, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Shou said, "If I hear the Way at dawn, I may die at dusk without regret."

sentences.zh: 遂即皇帝位，改國號曰漢，大赦，改元漢興。

translations.literal: He then ascended the imperial throne, changed the state name to Han, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Hanxing.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the throne, changed the state name to Han, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Hanxing.

sentences.zh: 以安車束帛征龔壯為太師。

translations.literal: With a carriage of honor and silks he summoned Gong Zhuang as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Gong Zhuang as Grand Preceptor with a carriage of honor and silks.

sentences.zh: 壯誓不仕，壽所贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Zhuang swore he would not serve; none of the gifts Shou sent did he accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang swore he would not serve and accepted none of Shou's gifts.

sentences.zh: 壽改立宗廟，追尊父驤曰獻皇帝，母昝氏曰皇太后。

translations.literal: Shou established a new ancestral temple and posthumously honored his father Xiang as Emperor Xian and his mother Lady Zan as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Shou built a new ancestral temple and posthumously honored his father Xiang as Emperor Xian and his mother Lady Zan as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 立妃閆氏為皇后，世子勢為皇太子。

translations.literal: He made his consort Lady Yan empress and his heir Shi crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his consort Lady Yan empress and his heir Shi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 更以舊廟為大成廟，凡諸制度，多所改易。

translations.literal: He converted the old temple into the Great Completion Temple and changed many institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the old temple into the Temple of Great Completion and altered many institutions.

sentences.zh: 以董皎為相國，羅恆為尚書令，解思明為廣漢太守，任調為鎮北將軍、梁州刺史，李弈為西夷校尉，從子權為寧州刺史。

translations.literal: He made Dong Jiao Chancellor of State, Luo Heng Director of the Masters of Writing, Xie Siming Administrator of Guanghan, Ren Diao Pacification-of-the-North General and Governor of Liang, Li Yi Colonel of the Western Yi, and his nephew Quan Governor of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Dong Jiao Chancellor of State, Luo Heng Director of the Masters of Writing, Xie Siming Administrator of Guanghan, Ren Diao Pacification-of-the-North General and Governor of Liang, Li Yi Colonel of the Western Yi, and his nephew Quan Governor of Ning.

sentences.zh: 公、卿、州、郡，悉用其僚佐代之；

translations.literal: Dukes, ministers, provinces, and commanderies were all staffed with his own followers in place of the old officials;
translations.idiomatic: He replaced every duke, minister, provincial governor, and prefect with his own men;

sentences.zh: 成氏舊臣、近親及六郡士人，皆見疏斥。

translations.literal: the old ministers of the Cheng clan, close kin, and gentry of the six commanderies were all pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: and pushed aside the old Cheng ministers, close kin, and gentry of the six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 邛都公期歎曰：「天下主乃為小縣公，不如死！」

translations.literal: The Duke of Qiongdu Qi sighed and said, "The lord of all under Heaven reduced to a petty county duke—better to die!"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Qiongdu Qi sighed and said, "The ruler of the realm reduced to a petty county duke—I would rather die!"

sentences.zh: 五月，縊而卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he hanged himself and died.

sentences.zh: 壽謚曰幽公，葬以王禮。

translations.literal: Shou gave him the posthumous title Duke You and buried him with royal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shou gave him the posthumous title Duke You and buried him with royal honors.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎以燕王皝不會趙兵攻段遼而自專其利，欲伐之。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao, because King Murong Huang of Yan had not joined Zhao's campaign against Duan Liao but kept the gains for himself, wished to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao, angry that Murong Huang had not joined the campaign against Duan Liao but kept the spoils for himself, planned to attack Yan.

sentences.zh: 太史令趙攬諫曰：「歲星守燕分，師必無功。」

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan remonstrated, saying, "The Year Star holds the Yan asterism; the army will surely achieve nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan warned him: "The Year Star stands in the Yan sector. Your army will not succeed."

sentences.zh: 虎怒，鞭之。

translations.literal: Hu was enraged and had him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Hu flew into a rage and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 皝聞之，嚴兵設備：罷六卿，納言，常伯，冗騎常侍官。

translations.literal: When Huang heard of this, he tightened military preparations: he abolished the offices of the Six Ministers, Supplicating Voice, Regular Baron, and Supernumerary Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang heard of this, he mobilized for war and abolished the posts of the Six Ministers, Supplicating Voice, Regular Baron, and Supernumerary Cavalry Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 趙戎卒數十萬，燕人震恐。

translations.literal: Zhao fielded several hundred thousand soldiers; the people of Yan were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao marshaled several hundred thousand troops, and the people of Yan were terrified.

sentences.zh: 皝謂內史高詡曰：「將若之何？」

translations.literal: Huang said to Interior Secretary Gao Xu, "What are we to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang asked his interior secretary Gao Xu, "What shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「趙兵雖強，然不足憂，但堅守以拒之，無能為也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Though the Zhao army is strong, there is nothing to worry about; only hold firm and resist them, and they can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Gao answered, "The Zhao army is strong, but there is no need to fear. Hold the walls and they can do nothing against us."

sentences.zh: 虎遣使四出，招誘民夷，燕成周內史崔燾、居就令游泓、武原令常霸、東夷校尉封抽、護軍宋晃等皆應之，凡得三十六城。

translations.literal: Hu sent envoys in all directions to win over the people and tribes; Yan's Interior Secretary of Chengzou Cui Tao, Magistrate of Jujiu You Hong, Magistrate of Wuyuan Chang Ba, Colonel of the Eastern Yi Feng Chou, Protector of the Army Song Huang, and others all responded, and in all thirty-six cities were gained.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent envoys in every direction to win over the people and tribes. Cui Tao, interior secretary of Chengzou; You Hong, magistrate of Jujiu; Chang Ba, magistrate of Wuyuan; Feng Chou, colonel of the Eastern Yi; Song Huang, protector of the army; and others all submitted. In all, thirty-six cities went over to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 泓，邃之兄子也。

translations.literal: Hong was a nephew of You Sui's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a nephew of You Sui.

sentences.zh: 冀陽流寓之士共殺太守宋燭以降於趙。

translations.literal: Exiled gentlemen of Jiyang together killed Administrator Song Zhu and surrendered to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled gentlemen of Jiyang killed Administrator Song Zhu and surrendered to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 燭，晃之從兄也。

translations.literal: Zhu was a cousin of Huang's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was a cousin of Song Huang's.

sentences.zh: 營丘內史鮮于屈亦遣使降趙。

translations.literal: Interior Secretary of Yingqiu Xianyu Qu also sent envoys to surrender to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Qu, interior secretary of Yingqiu, also sent envoys to surrender to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 武寧令廣平孫興曉諭吏民共收屈，數其罪而殺之，閉城拒守。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wuning Sun Xing of Guangping persuaded officials and people together to seize Qu, recounted his crimes, and killed him, then shut the city gates and held out.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xing of Guangping, magistrate of Wuning, rallied the officials and people to seize Qu, condemned his crimes, and executed him, then shut the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮令昌黎孫泳帥眾拒趙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chaoxian Sun Yong of Changli led the people to resist Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong of Changli, magistrate of Chaoxian, led his people in resistance to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 大姓王清等密謀應趙，泳收斬之；

translations.literal: Great clansmen Wang Qing and others secretly plotted to join Zhao; Yong arrested and executed them;
translations.idiomatic: Leading clansmen Wang Qing and others secretly plotted to join Zhao. Yong seized and executed them;

sentences.zh: 同謀數百人惶怖請罪，泳皆釋之，與同拒守。

translations.literal: several hundred co-conspirators, terrified, begged forgiveness; Yong released them all and together they held out.
translations.idiomatic: and when several hundred co-conspirators begged forgiveness in terror, he pardoned them all and they held the city with him.

sentences.zh: 樂浪太守鞠彭以境內皆叛，選鄉里壯士二百餘人共還棘城。

translations.literal: Administrator of Lelang Ju Peng, seeing the whole territory in revolt, selected more than two hundred stalwart men of his home district and returned with them to Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Peng, administrator of Lelang, found his whole territory in revolt. He chose more than two hundred stalwarts from his home district and marched back to Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 戊子，趙兵進逼棘城。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the Zhao army advanced and pressed Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the Zhao army advanced on Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝欲出亡，帳下將慕輿根諫曰：「趙強我弱，大王一舉足則趙之氣勢遂成，使趙人收略國民，兵強谷足，不可復敵。

translations.literal: King Murong Huang wished to flee; his officer Murong Gen remonstrated, saying, "Zhao is strong and we are weak. If Your Majesty takes one step, Zhao's momentum will be complete, and they will gather and plunder our people; with strong troops and full granaries, they will be impossible to face again.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang thought of fleeing. His officer Murong Gen urged him: "Zhao is strong and we are weak. If you take one step from this city, Zhao's momentum will be complete. They will sweep up our people, fill their granaries, and we will never be able to face them again.

sentences.zh: 竊意趙人正欲大王如此耳，奈何入其計中乎？

translations.literal: I suspect the Zhao men want exactly this from Your Majesty—why fall into their scheme?
translations.idiomatic: I believe the Zhao want nothing more than for you to do exactly that. Why walk into their trap?

sentences.zh: 今固守堅城，其勢百倍，縱其急攻，猶足支持，觀形察變，間出求利。

translations.literal: Now if we hold this strong city, our position is a hundred times stronger; even if they press the attack fiercely, we can still hold out, watch the situation, seize opportunities, and sally forth when profit offers.
translations.idiomatic: Hold this strong city and our position is a hundred times the stronger. Even if they press the attack, we can endure, watch how matters shift, and strike when the moment offers profit.

sentences.zh: 如事之不濟，不失於走，奈何望風委去，為必亡之理乎！」

translations.literal: If matters do not succeed, we still lose nothing by fleeing—why yield at the first sign and abandon all, as though defeat were certain!"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, we can still flee—but why surrender at the first alarm, as if defeat were certain!"

sentences.zh: 皝乃止，然猶懼形於色。

translations.literal: Huang then stopped, but fear still showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Huang held his ground, but fear still showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 玄菟太守河間劉佩曰：「今強寇在外，眾心恟懼，事之安危，繫於一人。

translations.literal: Administrator of Xuantu Liu Pei of Hejian said, "Now a powerful enemy is outside; the people's hearts are alarmed and afraid. The safety of the affair hangs on one man.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pei, administrator of Xuantu, said, "A powerful enemy stands outside the walls and the people are terrified. Everything depends on you alone.

sentences.zh: 大王此際無所推委，當自強以厲將士，不宜示弱。

translations.literal: At this moment Your Majesty has no one to whom to pass responsibility; you should strengthen yourself to hearten the officers and soldiers and should not show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: You cannot pass this burden to anyone else. You must steel yourself and hearten your men—not show weakness.

sentences.zh: 事急矣，臣請出擊之，縱無大捷，足以安眾。」

translations.literal: The matter is urgent; your servant asks leave to sally forth and attack them. Even without a great victory, it will be enough to steady the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The crisis is upon us. Let me lead a sortie. Even without a great victory, it will steady the army."

sentences.zh: 乃將敢死數百騎出沖趙兵，所向披靡，斬獲而還，於是士氣百倍。

translations.literal: He then led several hundred dare-to-die cavalry out in a charge against the Zhao army; wherever they went they swept all before them, took heads and captives, and returned; thus morale doubled a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: He led several hundred dare-to-die horsemen in a charge that broke the Zhao ranks. They cut down the enemy and returned with captives, and morale soared.

sentences.zh: 皝問計於封弈，對曰：「石虎凶虐已甚，民神共疾，禍敗之至，其何日之有！

translations.literal: Huang asked Feng Yi for counsel; he replied, "Shi Hu's cruelty and tyranny have already reached their limit; the people and the spirits alike detest him. When disaster and defeat will come—how many days can remain!
translations.idiomatic: Huang asked Feng Yi for advice. Feng Yi said, "Shi Hu's cruelty has gone as far as it can. Men and spirits alike hate him. His fall cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 今空國遠來，攻守勢異，戎馬雖強，無能為患；

translations.literal: Now they have emptied their state to come from afar; the situations of attack and defense differ; though their war-horses are strong, they cannot become a calamity;
translations.idiomatic: They have emptied their realm to march so far. Attack and defense favor us differently. Their cavalry is strong, but they cannot harm us;

sentences.zh: 頓兵積日，釁隙自生，但堅守以俟之耳。」

translations.literal: with troops halted day after day, rifts will arise of themselves; only hold firm and wait for them."
translations.idiomatic: if we hold out, their army will fray of its own accord. We need only stand firm and wait."

sentences.zh: 皝意乃安。

translations.literal: Huang's mind was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Huang took heart.

sentences.zh: 或說皝降，皝曰：「孤方取天下，何謂降也！」

translations.literal: Some urged Huang to surrender; Huang said, "I am just now taking all under Heaven—what talk is this of surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to surrender. Huang said, "I am on the verge of taking the realm—why speak of surrender?"

sentences.zh: 趙兵四面蟻附緣城，慕輿根等晝夜力戰，凡十餘日，趙兵不能克，壬辰，引退。

translations.literal: The Zhao army swarmed up the walls on all sides like ants; Murong Gen and others fought day and night with all their strength for more than ten days, and the Zhao army could not take the city; on renchen they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao army swarmed the walls on every side. Murong Gen and the others fought day and night for more than ten days until the Zhao forces could not take the city. On renchen they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皝遣其子恪帥二千騎追擊之，趙兵大敗，斬獲三萬餘級。

translations.literal: Huang sent his son Ke with two thousand cavalry in pursuit; the Zhao army was routed utterly, and more than thirty thousand heads and captives were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Huang sent his son Ke with two thousand horse in pursuit. The Zhao army was shattered, with more than thirty thousand killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 趙諸軍皆棄甲逃潰，惟游擊將軍石閔一軍獨全。

translations.literal: All the Zhao armies cast off their armor and fled in disorder; only Mobile Campaign General Shi Min's army remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Every Zhao unit threw off its armor and fled—only Mobile Campaign General Shi Min's command came back whole.

sentences.zh: 閔名瞻，內黃人，本姓冉，趙主勒破陳午，獲之，命虎養以為子。

translations.literal: Min's personal name was Zhan; he was a man of Neihuang, originally surnamed Ran. When Zhao's ruler Le broke Chen Wu, he was captured and Hu ordered Hu to rear him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Min, personal name Zhan, was from Neihuang and originally surnamed Ran. When Zhao's founder Le defeated Chen Wu, he was taken captive and Hu was ordered to rear him as a son.

sentences.zh: 閔驍勇善戰，多策略。

translations.literal: Min was fierce and brave in battle and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce in battle and cunning in counsel.

sentences.zh: 虎愛之，比於諸孫。

translations.literal: Hu loved him and treated him like his own grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Hu favored him as he did his own grandsons.

sentences.zh: 虎還鄴，以劉群為中書令，盧諶為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Hu returned to Ye and made Liu Qun Director of the Palace Secretariat and Lu Chen Deputy Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hu returned to Ye and appointed Liu Qun Director of the Palace Secretariat and Lu Chen his deputy.

sentences.zh: 蒲洪以功拜使持節、都督六夷諸軍事、冠軍大將軍，封西平郡公。

translations.literal: Pu Hong, for his merit, was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Six Yi Armies, Champion Grand General, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit, Pu Hong was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of the Six Yi armies, Champion Grand General, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 石閔言於虎曰：「蒲洪雄俊，得將士死力，諸子皆有非常之才，且握強兵五萬，屯據近畿；

translations.literal: Shi Min said to Hu, "Pu Hong is heroic and outstanding and commands the officers and soldiers' utmost loyalty; all his sons have extraordinary talent; moreover he holds a strong army of fifty thousand and is encamped near the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min told Hu, "Pu Hong is formidable and commands absolute loyalty. His sons are all exceptional men, and he holds fifty thousand troops near the capital;

sentences.zh: 宜密除之，以安社稷。」

translations.literal: he should be secretly removed to secure the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: you should remove him in secret to secure the realm."

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「吾方倚其父子以取吳、蜀，奈何殺之！」

translations.literal: Hu said, "I am just now relying on him and his sons to take Wu and Shu—how can I kill them!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "I am counting on him and his sons to conquer Wu and Shu—why would I kill them?"

sentences.zh: 待之愈厚。

translations.literal: He treated them all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: He treated them with even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝分兵討諸叛城，皆下之。

translations.literal: King Murong Huang divided his forces to attack the rebel cities, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang sent forces against the rebel cities and recovered them all.

sentences.zh: 拓境至凡城。

translations.literal: He extended his borders to Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He extended his borders to Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 崔燾、常霸奔鄴，封抽、宋晃、游漲奔高句麗。

translations.literal: Cui Tao and Chang Ba fled to Ye; Feng Chou, Song Huang, and You Hong fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tao and Chang Ba fled to Ye; Feng Chou, Song Huang, and You Hong fled to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 皝賞鞠彭、慕輿根等而治諸叛者，誅滅甚眾；

translations.literal: Huang rewarded Ju Peng, Murong Gen, and others and punished the rebels; the executions were very numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Huang rewarded Ju Peng, Murong Gen, and others and punished the rebels with mass executions;

sentences.zh: 功曹劉翔為之申理，多所全活。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Liu Xiang pleaded on their behalf and many lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Liu Xiang pleaded for mercy and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 趙之攻棘城也，燕右司李洪之弟普以為棘城必敗，勸洪出避禍。

translations.literal: When Zhao attacked Jicheng, the younger brother Pu of Li Hong of the Yan Right Bureau thought Jicheng would surely fall and urged Hong to flee and avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhao's siege of Jicheng, Pu, younger brother of Li Hong of the Yan Right Bureau, believed the city would fall and urged Hong to flee.

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「天道幽遠，人事難知。

translations.literal: Hong said, "The way of Heaven is obscure and human affairs hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "Heaven's ways are obscure and human affairs uncertain.

sentences.zh: 且當委任，勿輕動取悔。」

translations.literal: For now one should entrust oneself to duty and not lightly act and invite regret."
translations.idiomatic: For now we must do our duty and not act rashly and regret it."

sentences.zh: 普固請不已，洪曰：「卿意見明審者，當自行之。

translations.literal: Pu pressed his request without cease; Hong said, "If your view is so clear and decisive, go yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Pu kept pressing him. Hong said, "If you are so sure, go yourself.

sentences.zh: 吾受慕容氏大恩，義無去就，當效死於此耳。」

translations.literal: I have received great favor from the Murong clan; in righteousness I cannot leave or stay—I should die here."
translations.idiomatic: I owe the Murong clan too much to leave. I will die here."

sentences.zh: 與普流涕而訣。

translations.literal: He and Pu wept and took leave of each other.
translations.idiomatic: He and Pu wept and parted.

sentences.zh: 普遂降趙，從趙軍南歸，死於喪亂；

translations.literal: Pu then surrendered to Zhao and followed the Zhao army south; he died in the turmoil of mourning and disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Pu surrendered to Zhao and marched south with the Zhao army. He died in the chaos of the times;

sentences.zh: 洪由是以忠篤著名。

translations.literal: and because of this Hong became famous for loyalty and steadfastness.
translations.idiomatic: and Hong won renown for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎遣渡遼將軍曹伏將青州之眾戍海島，運谷三百萬斛以給之；

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao sent Crossing-Liao General Cao Fu to lead the masses of Qing Province to garrison the sea islands, shipping three million hu of grain to supply them;
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu sent Crossing-Liao General Cao Fu with the people of Qing Province to garrison the sea islands and shipped three million hu of grain to supply them;

sentences.zh: 又以船三百艘運谷三十萬斛詣高句麗，使典農中郎將王典帥眾萬餘屯田海濱；

translations.literal: he also used three hundred ships to transport three hundred thousand hu of grain to Goguryeo and had Director of Agriculture Central Commandant Wang Dian lead more than ten thousand men to farm by the seashore;
translations.idiomatic: he also sent three hundred ships with three hundred thousand hu of grain to Goguryeo and had Director of Agriculture Wang Dian lead more than ten thousand men to farm the coast;

sentences.zh: 又令青州造船千艘，以謀擊燕。

translations.literal: and he ordered Qing Province to build a thousand ships to plan an attack on Yan.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Qing Province to build a thousand ships for another strike at Yan.

sentences.zh: 趙太子宣帥步騎二萬擊朔方鮮卑斛摩頭，破之，斬首四萬餘級。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of Zhao led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the Shangfang Xianbei Huluotou, defeated them, and took more than forty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xuan of Zhao led twenty thousand foot and horse against the Shangfang Xianbei Huluotou, defeated them, and took more than forty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 冀州八郡大蝗，趙司隸請坐守宰。

translations.literal: Eight commanderies of Ji Province suffered great locusts; Zhao's Director of the Masters of Writing requested that the guarding governors be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies of Ji Province suffered a great locust plague. Zhao's Director of the Masters of Writing asked that the local governors be punished.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎曰：「此朕失敗所致，而欲委咎守宰，豈罪己之意邪！

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao said, "This is caused by my own failures, yet you wish to shift blame onto the governors—is this the meaning of blaming oneself!
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu said, "This is my own failure. To blame the governors—is that how a ruler takes responsibility?

sentences.zh: 司隸不進讜言，佐朕不逮，而欲妄陷無辜，可白衣領職！」

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing does not advance loyal remonstrance to help me where I fall short, yet wishes to falsely harm the innocent—you may serve in plain dress!"
translations.idiomatic: You fail to counsel me honestly, yet would ruin innocent men. You may serve in plain dress!"

sentences.zh: 虎使襄城公涉歸、上庸公日歸帥眾戍長安。

translations.literal: Hu sent Duke of Xiangcheng Shegui and Duke of Shangyong Rigui to lead troops to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Duke of Xiangcheng Shegui and Duke of Shangyong Rigui to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 二歸告鎮西將軍石廣私樹恩澤，潛謀不軌；

translations.literal: The two Guis reported that Western Campaign General Shi Guang was privately bestowing favors and secretly plotting rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: The two Guis reported that Western Campaign General Shi Guang was currying favor and plotting rebellion;

sentences.zh: 虎追廣至鄴，殺之。

translations.literal: Hu pursued Guang to Ye and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu summoned Guang to Ye and executed him.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以司徒導為太傅，都督中外諸軍事；

translations.literal: On yiwei, Director of the Masters of Writing Dao was made Grand Tutor and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Dao was made Grand Tutor and commander of all armies at home and abroad;

sentences.zh: 郗鑒為太尉，庾亮為司空。

translations.literal: Xi Jian was made Grand Commandant and Yu Liang Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian was made Grand Commandant and Yu Liang Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六月，以尋為丞相，罷司徒官以並丞相府。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Dao was made Chancellor and the office of Director of the Masters of Writing was abolished and merged into the chancellor's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Dao was made Chancellor; the office of Director of the Masters of Writing was abolished and merged into the chancellor's establishment.

sentences.zh: 導性寬厚，委任諸將趙胤、賈寧等，多不奉法，大臣患之。

translations.literal: Dao was by nature generous and broad; he entrusted various generals Zhao Yin, Jia Ning, and others, who for the most part did not observe the law—the great ministers were troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was generous by nature and left his generals Zhao Yin, Jia Ning, and others to their own devices. Many broke the law, and the ministers were troubled.

sentences.zh: 庾亮與郗鑒箋曰：「主上自八九歲以及成人，入則在宮人之手，出則唯武官、小人，讀書無從受音句，顧問未嘗遇君子。

translations.literal: Yu Liang wrote to Xi Jian, saying, "From the time the Son of Heaven was eight or nine years old until he came of age, within the palace he was in the hands of palace women; outside he saw only military officers and petty men. In reading books he had no one from whom to receive phrases and lines; in consultation he never met a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang wrote to Xi Jian: "From childhood the emperor was raised by palace women within and saw only soldiers and petty men without. He had no proper teachers and never heard counsel from a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 秦政欲愚其黔首，天下猶知不可，況欲愚其主哉！

translations.literal: Qin Zheng wished to make fools of the black-haired masses, yet all under Heaven still knew it could not be done—how much less can one make a fool of the ruler!
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zheng tried to keep the people ignorant, and the realm knew it was wrong—how much worse to keep the ruler ignorant!

sentences.zh: 人主春秋既盛，宜復子明辟。

translations.literal: The ruler's spring years are already full; he should restore the Son to enlightened rule.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has come of age. He should rule in his own right.

sentences.zh: 不稽首歸政，甫居師傅之尊，多養無賴之士；

translations.literal: Without bowing the head and returning government, he has only just occupied the exalted post of tutor and keeps many worthless fellows;
translations.idiomatic: Instead of yielding power, he clings to his post as tutor and surrounds himself with worthless men;

sentences.zh: 公與下官並荷托付之重，大奸不掃，何以見先帝於地下乎！」

translations.literal: you and I alike bear the weight of entrustment—if we do not sweep away great traitors, how can we face the Former Emperor underground!"
translations.idiomatic: we were both entrusted with the realm. If we do not remove this great evil, how can we face the late emperor?"

sentences.zh: 欲共起兵廢導，鑒不聽。

translations.literal: They wished together to raise troops and depose Dao; Jian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to raise troops and depose Dao, but Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 南蠻校尉陶稱，侃之子也，以亮謀語導。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Southern Man Tao Cheng, son of Kan, told Dao of Liang's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng, son of Kan and colonel of the Southern Man, told Dao of Liang's plot.

sentences.zh: 或勸導密為之備，導曰：「吾與元規休戚是同，悠悠之談，宜絕智者之口。

translations.literal: Some urged Dao to prepare in secret; Dao said, "Yuangui and I share weal and woe alike; idle talk of this sort should be cut off at the mouths of the wise.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Dao to take precautions. Dao said, "Yuangui and I are bound by kinship. Idle gossip should stop with the wise.

sentences.zh: 則如君言，元規若來，吾便角巾還第，復何懼哉！」

translations.literal: Moreover, as you say, if Yuangui comes, I shall simply put on my kerchief and return to my estate—what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: And if Yuangui does come, I will simply retire to my estate in my kerchief. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 又與稱書，以為：「庾公帝之元舅，宜善事之！」

translations.literal: He also wrote to Cheng, thinking, "Duke Yu is the emperor's senior maternal uncle; he should be well treated!"
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Cheng: "Duke Yu is the emperor's senior maternal uncle. Treat him well!"

sentences.zh: 征西參軍孫盛密諫亮曰：「王公常有世外之懷，豈肯為凡人事邪！

translations.literal: Western Campaign staff officer Sun Sheng secretly remonstrated with Liang, saying, "The Duke of Zhou has long had a mind set beyond the world—how would he stoop to the affairs of ordinary men!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng, on the western campaign staff, warned Liang in secret: "The Duke of Zhou has long had a mind above worldly things. Would he trouble himself with vulgar intrigue?

sentences.zh: 此必佞邪之徒欲間內外耳。」

translations.literal: This must be slanderous petty men wishing to set inner and outer at odds."
translations.idiomatic: This must be slander from men who want to divide court and camp."

sentences.zh: 亮乃止。

translations.literal: Liang then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Liang abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 盛，楚之孫也。

translations.literal: Sheng was a grandson of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was a grandson of Chu.

sentences.zh: 是時亮雖居外鎮，而遙執朝廷之權，既據上流，擁強兵，趣勢者多歸之。

translations.literal: At this time, though Liang held an outer commandery, he remotely wielded court power; having the upper reaches and strong troops, many who sought advantage turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liang held a frontier post, he controlled the court from afar. With the upper Yangzi and a strong army, men of ambition flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 導內不能平，常遇西風塵起，舉扇自蔽，徐曰：「元規塵污人！」

translations.literal: Dao could not be at peace within; whenever the west wind raised dust, he would lift his fan to shield himself and say slowly, "Yuangui's dust soils men!"
translations.idiomatic: Dao could not contain his resentment. When the west wind blew dust, he would raise his fan and murmur, "Yuangui's dust fouls a man!"

sentences.zh: 導以江夏李充為丞相掾。

translations.literal: Dao made Li Chong of Jiangxia a staff officer of the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Dao appointed Li Chong of Jiangxia to his staff.

sentences.zh: 充以時俗崇尚浮虛，乃著《學箴》。

translations.literal: Chong, seeing the age's fashion exalting empty frivolity, composed the "Admonition on Learning."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the age's taste for empty frivolity, Chong wrote the Admonition on Learning.

sentences.zh: 以為老子云「絕仁棄義，民復孝慈，」豈仁義之道絕，然後孝慈乃生哉？

translations.literal: He thought that Laozi said, "abolish benevolence and discard righteousness, and the people will return to filial piety and kindness"—was it that the way of benevolence and righteousness was cut off, and only then did filial piety and kindness arise?
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, "Abolish benevolence and discard righteousness, and the people will return to filial piety and kindness." Did he mean that only when benevolence and righteousness were gone would filial piety appear?

sentences.zh: 蓋患乎情仁義者寡，而利仁義者眾，將寄責於聖人而遣累乎陳跡也。

translations.literal: Rather, he feared that those who were moved by benevolence and righteousness were few while those who profited from them were many, and wished to lodge responsibility with the sages while shedding the burden of old traces.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, he feared that few were moved by benevolence and righteousness while many profited from them, and wished to lay the burden on the sages while shedding the traces of the past.

sentences.zh: 凡人見形者眾，及道者鮮，逐跡逾篤，離本逾遠。

translations.literal: Ordinary men who see forms are many; those who attain the Way are few—chasing traces grows ever more earnest, leaving the root ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: Most men see only the form; few grasp the Way. The more they chase traces, the farther they leave the root.

sentences.zh: 故作《學箴》以祛其蔽曰：「名之攸彰，道之攸廢；

translations.literal: Therefore he made the "Admonition on Learning" to dispel this blindness, saying, "Where fame is displayed, the Way is abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: So he wrote the Admonition to clear this blindness: "Where fame is displayed, the Way is abandoned;

sentences.zh: 及損所隆，乃崇所替。

translations.literal: when what was lowered is exalted, what was honored is cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: what was lowered is exalted, and what was honored is cast aside.

sentences.zh: 非仁無以長物，非義無以齊恥，仁義固不可遠，去其害仁義者而已。」

translations.literal: Without benevolence one cannot nurture things; without righteousness one cannot align shame—benevolence and righteousness surely cannot be far removed; only remove what harms benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Without benevolence nothing can flourish; without righteousness shame cannot be ordered. Benevolence and righteousness cannot be cast away—only what harms them must go."

sentences.zh: 漢李弈從兄廣漢太守乾告大臣謀廢立。

translations.literal: In Han, Li Yi's elder cousin by the same clan, Administrator of Guanghan Gan, reported that the great ministers were plotting deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Li Yi's cousin Gan, administrator of Guanghan, accused the great ministers of plotting to depose the ruler.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，漢主壽使其子廣與大臣盟於前殿，徙乾為漢嘉太守；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Han's ruler Shou had his son Guang swear an oath with the great ministers in the front hall and transferred Gan to be Administrator of Hanjia;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Shou of Han had his son Guang swear an oath with the ministers in the front hall and transferred Gan to be administrator of Hanjia;

sentences.zh: 以李閎為荊州刺史，鎮巴郡。

translations.literal: he made Li Hong Governor of Jing and stationed him in Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: he made Li Hong governor of Jing and stationed him in Ba.

sentences.zh: 閎，恭之子也。

translations.literal: Hong was a son of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a son of Gong.

sentences.zh: 八月，蜀中久雨，百姓饑疫，壽命群臣極言得失。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, in Shu there had long been rain; the people suffered famine and pestilence; Shou ordered the ministers to speak freely of gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, long rains brought famine and pestilence to Shu. Shou ordered his ministers to speak freely of what had gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 龔壯上封事稱：「陛下起兵之初，上指星辰，昭告天地，歃血盟眾，舉國稱籓，天應人悅，大功克集。

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang submitted a sealed memorial saying, "When Your Majesty first raised troops, you pointed to the stars above and proclaimed to Heaven and Earth below, smeared blood and swore with the masses, and the whole state declared itself a vassal of Jin; Heaven responded and men rejoiced, and great achievement was gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang submitted a sealed memorial: "When you first raised your banner, you pointed to the stars, proclaimed your oath to Heaven and Earth, and the whole state declared itself Jin's vassal. Heaven approved and great success followed.

sentences.zh: 而論者未諭，權宜稱制。

translations.literal: Yet those who discuss the matter have not understood and, as an expedient, styled you emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men still do not understand and insist on calling you emperor as an expedient.

sentences.zh: 今淫雨百日，饑疫並臻，天其或者將以監示陛下故也。

translations.literal: Now a hundred days of excessive rain, famine and pestilence together have come—perhaps Heaven intends thereby to show Your Majesty a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Now a hundred days of rain have brought famine and pestilence together. Perhaps Heaven means to warn you.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜遵前盟，推奉建康，彼必不愛高爵重位以報大功；

translations.literal: This humble one thinks you should follow the former oath, support and serve Jiankang—they will surely not begrudge high rank and weighty posts to repay great merit;
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to honor your former oath and submit to Jiankang. They will not begrudge high rank to repay your service;

sentences.zh: 雖降階一等，而子孫無窮，永保福祚，不亦休哉！

translations.literal: though you descend one step in rank, your descendants will be endless and blessings and emoluments will be forever preserved—is this not excellent!
translations.idiomatic: though you step down one rank, your line will endure forever. Would that not be better?

sentences.zh: 論者或言二州附晉則榮，六郡人事之不便。

translations.literal: Some who discuss say that if the two provinces submit to Jin it will be glory, but the six commanderies will find serving inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that the two provinces would gain glory by submitting to Jin, but the six commanderies would suffer.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫述在蜀，羈客用事，劉備在蜀，楚士多貴。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongsun Shu was in Shu and detained guests to hold office; Liu Bei was in Shu and Chu men were mostly honored.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Shu held Shu, outsiders ruled. When Liu Bei held Shu, men from Chu rose high.

sentences.zh: 及吳、鄧西伐，舉國屠滅，寧分客主！

translations.literal: When Wu and Deng marched west, the whole state was slaughtered to extinction—what matter native or guest!
translations.idiomatic: When Wu and Deng marched west, the whole state was slaughtered—native and guest alike!

sentences.zh: 論者不達安固之基，苟惜名位，以為劉氏守令方仕州郡；

translations.literal: Those who discuss do not grasp the foundation of security and solid rule but cling to name and rank, thinking that Liu's prefects and magistrates were just then serving in provinces and commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: They do not see what makes a state secure but cling to titles, as if Liu's officials were merely serving local posts;

sentences.zh: 曾不知彼乃國亡主易，豈同今日義舉，主榮臣顯哉！

translations.literal: they do not know that then the state perished and the ruler changed—how can that compare with today's righteous undertaking, where the ruler is honored and ministers displayed!
translations.idiomatic: they forget that then the state fell and the ruler changed. How can that compare with today's righteous act, where ruler and ministers both gain?

sentences.zh: 論者又謂臣當為法正。

translations.literal: Others also say your servant should be a Fa Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Others say I should play Fa Zheng.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙陛下大恩，恣臣所安；

translations.literal: Your servant has received Your Majesty's great favor and you allow me what brings me peace;
translations.idiomatic: I have received your great favor and you let me live as I choose;

sentences.zh: 至於榮祿，無問漢、晉，臣皆不處，復何為傚法正乎！」

translations.literal: as for glory and salary, whether Han or Jin, your servant will accept none—why then imitate Fa Zheng!"
translations.idiomatic: as for rank and salary, whether under Han or Jin I will accept none. Why should I imitate Fa Zheng?"

sentences.zh: 壽省書內慚，秘而不宣。

translations.literal: Shou, on reading the memorial, felt shame within but kept it secret and did not proclaim it.
translations.idiomatic: Shou read the memorial, felt ashamed within, and kept it secret.

sentences.zh: 九月，漢僕射任顏謀反，誅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Han's Vice Director Ren Yan plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Han's Vice Director Ren Yan plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 顏，任太后之弟也。

translations.literal: Yan was a younger brother of Empress Dowager Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Empress Dowager Ren's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 漢主壽因盡誅成主雄諸子。

translations.literal: Han's ruler Shou therefore executed all the sons of the former ruler Xiong of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shou of Han then executed all the sons of the former ruler Xiong of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，光祿勳顏含以老遜位。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Household Counsellor Yan Han yielded his post on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Household Counsellor Yan Han resigned on account of age.

sentences.zh: 論者以「王導帝之師傅，名位隆重，百僚宜為降禮。」

translations.literal: Discussants held that "Wang Dao is the emperor's teacher and mentor; his name and rank are eminent and weighty; all the officials ought to extend lowered courtesies to him."
translations.idiomatic: “Some argued that since Wang Dao was the emperor's teacher and his name and standing were so lofty, the whole court ought to show him special deference.”

sentences.zh: 太常馮懷以問含。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Feng Huai questioned Han about it.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies, Feng Huai, put the question to Yan Han.

sentences.zh: 含曰：「王公雖貴重，理無偏敬。

translations.literal: Han said, "Though the Duke of Wang is eminent and weighty, by principle there is no partial deference.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han replied, "However eminent Lord Wang may be, propriety does not call for special favor.

sentences.zh: 降禮之言，或是諸君事宜；

translations.literal: The talk of lowered courtesies is perhaps your gentlemen's concern;
translations.idiomatic: As for lowering one's courtesies—that may be your colleagues' business;

sentences.zh: 鄙人老矣，不識時務。」

translations.literal: I am old and do not understand the affairs of the time."
translations.idiomatic: I am an old man who no longer understands what the times require."

sentences.zh: 既而告人曰：「吾聞伐國不問仁人，向馮祖思問佞於我，我豈有邪德乎！」

translations.literal: Later he told others, "I have heard that when planning to attack a state one does not ask a man of benevolence; just now Feng Zusi asked me about flattery—do I possess wicked virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: Later he told others, "They say you do not consult a good man when plotting to attack a country. Feng just now asked me about sycophancy—as if I were some corrupt adviser!"

sentences.zh: 郭璞嘗遇含，欲為之筮。

translations.literal: The diviner Guo Pu once met Han and wished to cast the stalks for him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once encountered Yan Han and offered to perform a divination for him.

sentences.zh: 含曰：「年在天，位在人。

translations.literal: Han said, "Years belong to Heaven; position belongs to man.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han said, "How long one lives is Heaven's doing; what rank one holds is one's own.

sentences.zh: 修己而天不與者，命也；

translations.literal: One cultivates oneself yet Heaven does not grant—this is fate;
translations.idiomatic: If you refine yourself and Heaven still withholds its favor, that is fate;

sentences.zh: 守道而人不知者，性也；

translations.literal: One keeps the Way yet men do not know—this is one's nature;
translations.idiomatic: if you hold to the Way and others fail to recognize it, that is simply your temperament;

sentences.zh: 自有性命，無勞蓍龜。」

translations.literal: Life and fate are one's own; there is no need for milfoil and tortoise."
translations.idiomatic: Life and destiny are already determined—there is no need for divination with stalks and shells."

sentences.zh: 致仕二十餘年，年九十三而卒。

translations.literal: He had retired for more than twenty years and died at the age of ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He had been retired for over twenty years and died at ninety-three.

sentences.zh: 代王翳槐之弟什翼犍質於趙，翳槐疾病，命諸大人立之。

translations.literal: Shiyijian, younger brother of the Prince of Dai Yihui, was held hostage in Zhao; when Yihui fell ill he ordered the tribal elders to install him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Shiyijian, the Prince of Dai and younger brother of Yihui, was a hostage in Zhao. When Yihui fell gravely ill, he ordered the tribal elders to install Shiyijian as his successor.

sentences.zh: 翳槐卒，諸大人梁蓋等以新有大故，什翼犍在遠，來未可必；

translations.literal: When Yihui died, the elders Liang Gai and others, because there had just been a great bereavement and Shiyijian was far away and his arrival were countless on,
translations.idiomatic: When Yihui died, the tribal elders Liang Gai and others reasoned that with the realm in fresh mourning and Shiyijian still far away, his return was uncertain;

sentences.zh: 比其至，恐有變亂，謀更立君。

translations.literal: feared that by the time he arrived there might be disorder, and plotted to install another ruler.
translations.idiomatic: they feared unrest before he could arrive and plotted to choose another ruler.

sentences.zh: 而翳槐次弟屈，剛猛多詐，不如屈弟孤仁厚，乃相與殺屈而立孤。

translations.literal: Yihui's next younger brother Qu was fierce, brutal, and much given to deceit, and was not as good as Qu's younger brother Gu, who was solitary, benevolent, and generous; they therefore together killed Qu and installed Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Yihui's next younger brother Qu was fierce and treacherous, whereas Qu's younger brother Gu was gentle and magnanimous. The elders killed Qu and raised Gu instead.

sentences.zh: 孤不可，自詣鄴迎什翼犍，請身留為質；

translations.literal: Gu refused; he went in person to Ye to welcome Shiyijian and asked to remain behind as hostage;
translations.idiomatic: Gu refused the throne, went himself to Ye to bring Shiyijian back, and offered to stay behind as a hostage;

sentences.zh: 趙王虎義而俱遣之。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao, moved by righteousness, sent them both away.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao, admiring his integrity, released them both.

sentences.zh: 十一月，什翼犍即代王位於繁畤北，改元曰建國，分國之半以與孤。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Shiyijian took the throne of Dai north of Fanchi, changed the era name to Establishing the State, and gave half the realm to Gu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Tuoba Shiyijian was enthroned as Prince of Dai north of Fanchi, proclaimed the era name Establishing the State, and divided the realm in half, granting one portion to Gu.

sentences.zh: 初，代王猗盧既卒，國多內難，部落離散，拓跋氏寢衰。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Prince Yilu of Dai died, the state suffered many internal troubles and the tribes scattered; the house of Tuoba gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Yilu of Dai died, the realm was torn by internal strife and the tribes scattered; the house of Tuoba fell into decline.

sentences.zh: 及什翼犍立，雄勇有智略，能修祖業，國人附之，始置百官，分掌眾務。

translations.literal: When Shiyijian was installed, he was bold and brave, possessed of wisdom and strategy, able to restore the ancestral enterprise; the people of the state attached themselves to him, and he first established the hundred offices and divided them to manage the various affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shiyijian took the throne, his courage and strategic talent restored the ancestral enterprise. The people rallied to him, he established a full bureaucracy, and assigned offices to govern every branch of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 以代人燕鳳為長史，許謙為郎中令。

translations.literal: He made the man of Dai Yan Feng Chief Clerk and Xu Qian Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yan Feng of Dai as Chief Clerk and Xu Qian as Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 始制反逆、殺人、奸盜之法，號令明白，政事清簡，無系訊連逮之煩，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He first established laws against treason, murder, and theft and adultery; the orders were clear, government affairs were pure and simple, and there was none of the trouble of chained interrogations and extended arrests; the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He codified laws against treason, murder, and robbery; his edicts were clear, administration lean, and the people were spared the torment of endless interrogations and dragnet arrests.

sentences.zh: 於是東自濊貊，西及破落那，南距陰山，北盡沙漠，率皆歸服，有眾數十萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the east as far as the Wimo, west to Poluona, south to the Yin Mountains, and north to the desert sands, all submitted and were obedient; he had a following of several hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wimo in the east to Poluona in the west, from the Yin Mountains in the south to the desert sands in the north, the tribes submitted; his following numbered several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 十二月，段遼自密雲山遣使求迎於趙；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Duan Liao sent envoys from Mount Miyun to Zhao seeking to be received;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Duan Liao sent envoys from Mount Miyun to Zhao asking to be taken in;

sentences.zh: 既而中悔，復遣使求迎於燕。

translations.literal: then he repented midway and again sent envoys to Yan seeking to be received.
translations.idiomatic: but soon changed his mind and sent envoys to Yan instead, asking to be received there.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎遣征東將軍麻秋帥眾三萬迎之，敕秋曰：「受降如受敵，不可輕也。」

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao sent Eastern Campaigning General Ma Qiu to lead thirty thousand men to receive him, instructing Qiu, "Receiving a surrender is like receiving an enemy—one must not treat it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao dispatched Eastern Campaigning General Ma Qiu with thirty thousand men to escort him home, warning Qiu, "Accepting a surrender is like facing an enemy—you must not take it lightly.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左丞陽裕，遼之故臣，使為秋司馬。

translations.literal: He made Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Yu, a former minister of Liao, Qiu's Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and a former minister of Duan Liao, as Ma Qiu's Chief of Staff.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝自帥諸將軍迎遼，遼密與燕謀覆趙軍。

translations.literal: King Murong Huang of Yan personally led the generals to receive Liao; Liao secretly plotted with Yan to overthrow the Zhao army.
translations.idiomatic: King Murong Huang of Yan led his generals in person to receive Duan Liao, who secretly conspired with Yan to destroy the Zhao force.

sentences.zh: 皝遣慕容恪伏精騎七千於密雲山，大敗麻秋於三藏口，死者什六七。

translations.literal: Huang sent Murong Ke to lie in ambush with seven thousand elite cavalry on Mount Miyun and utterly defeated Ma Qiu at Sancang Pass; six or seven tenths of the dead were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang sent Murong Ke with seven thousand elite cavalry in ambush on Mount Miyun and routed Ma Qiu at Sancang Pass, killing sixty or seventy percent of his men.

sentences.zh: 秋步走得免，陽裕為燕所執。

translations.literal: Qiu escaped on foot; Yang Yu was captured by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu fled on foot. Yang Yu was taken by the Yan army.

sentences.zh: 趙將軍范陽鮮于亮失馬，步緣山不能進，因止，端坐；

translations.literal: The Zhao general Xianyu Liang of Fanyang lost his horse, climbed the mountain on foot and could not advance, and so stopped and sat upright;
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Liang of Fanyang, a Zhao general, lost his horse, struggled up the mountain on foot until he could go no farther, and simply stopped and sat upright;

sentences.zh: 燕兵環之，叱令起。

translations.literal: Yan soldiers surrounded him and shouted at him to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan soldiers surrounded him and ordered him to stand.

sentences.zh: 亮曰：「身是貴人，義不為小人所屈。

translations.literal: Liang said, "I am a man of rank; by principle I will not be bent by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Liang said, "I am a man of standing. I will not bow to the likes of you.

sentences.zh: 汝曹能殺亟殺，不能則去！」

translations.literal: If you can kill, kill at once; if not, then go away!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill me if you can. If not, be gone!"

sentences.zh: 亮儀觀豐偉，聲氣雄厲，燕兵憚之，不敢殺，以白皝。

translations.literal: Liang's bearing was imposing and his voice fierce and stern; the Yan soldiers feared him and did not dare kill him, and reported it to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's bearing was imposing and his voice thunderous. The Yan soldiers dared not kill him and reported the matter to Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 皝以馬迎之，與語，大悅，用為左常侍，以崔毖之女妻之。

translations.literal: Huang met him with a horse, spoke with him, and was greatly pleased; he employed him as Left Regular Attendant and gave him the daughter of Cui Bi in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang sent a horse for him, spoke with him, and was greatly impressed. He made him Left Regular Attendant and gave him Cui Bi's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 皝盡得段遼之眾。

translations.literal: Huang completely obtained Liao's forces.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang took over Duan Liao's entire force.

sentences.zh: 待遼以上賓之禮，以陽裕為郎中令。

translations.literal: He treated Liao with the courtesies due a highest guest and made Yang Yu Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Duan Liao as an honored guest of the highest rank and appointed Yang Yu Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎聞麻秋敗，怒，削其官爵。

translations.literal: When King Shi Hu of Zhao heard that Ma Qiu had been defeated, he was enraged and stripped him of rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: When King Shi Hu of Zhao learned of Ma Qiu's defeat, he flew into a rage and stripped him of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day xinchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙丑，廣州刺史鄧岳將兵擊漢寧州，漢建寧太守孟彥執其刺史霍彪以降。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day yichou, Governor of Guang Province Deng Yue led troops to attack Han's Ning Province; Han's Jianning Prefect Meng Yan seized his Inspector Huo Biao and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day yichou, Deng Yue, Governor of Guang Province, attacked Ning Province of Han. Meng Yan, Prefect of Jianning in Han, seized Inspector Huo Biao and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍庾亮欲開復中原，表桓宣為都督沔北前鋒諸軍事、司州刺史，鎮襄陽；

translations.literal: Western Campaigning General Yu Liang wished to reopen the recovery of the Central Plains and memorialized that Huan Xuan be made Commander of the Forward Forces North of the Mian and Inspector of Si Province, stationed at Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: Western Campaigning General Yu Liang sought to reopen the campaign to recover the Central Plains. He recommended Huan Xuan as Commander of the Forward Forces North of the Mian and Inspector of Si Province, to be stationed at Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 又表其弟臨川太守懌為監梁、雍二州諸軍事、染州刺史，鎮魏興；

translations.literal: he also memorialized that his younger brother Yi, Administrator of Linchuan, be made Supervisor of Military Affairs in Liang and Yong Provinces and Inspector of Liang Province, stationed at Weixing;
translations.idiomatic: he also recommended his younger brother Yi, Administrator of Linchuan, as Supervisor of Military Affairs in Liang and Yong Provinces and Inspector of Liang Province, stationed at Weixing;

sentences.zh: 西陽太守翼為南蠻校尉，領南郡太守，鎮江陵；

translations.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Yi as Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, concurrently Administrator of Nan Commandery, stationed at Jiangling;
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Administrator of Xiyang, as Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and concurrent Administrator of Nan Commandery, stationed at Jiangling;

sentences.zh: 皆假節。

translations.literal: all were granted provisional authority.
translations.idiomatic: Each appointment carried provisional military authority.

sentences.zh: 又請解豫州，以授征虜將軍毛寶。

translations.literal: He also requested to relinquish Yu Province and grant it to Eastern Campaigning General Mao Bao.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to surrender his post in Yu Province to Eastern Campaigning General Mao Bao.

sentences.zh: 詔以寶監揚州之江西諸軍事、豫州刺史，與西陽太守樊峻帥精兵萬人戍邾城。

translations.literal: An edict made Bao Supervisor of Military Affairs west of the Yangzi in Yang Province and Inspector of Yu Province; together with Administrator of Xiyang Fan Jun he led ten thousand elite troops to garrison Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Mao Bao Supervisor of Military Affairs west of the Yangzi in Yang Province and Inspector of Yu Province, and ordered him and Fan Jun, Administrator of Xiyang, to garrison Zhucheng with ten thousand elite troops.

sentences.zh: 以建威將軍陶稱為南中郎將、江夏相，入沔中。

translations.literal: Establishing Prestige General Tao Cheng was made General of the Southern Gentlemen and Chancellor of Jiangxia and entered the Mian region.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng, Establishing Prestige General, was made General of the Southern Gentlemen and Chancellor of Jiangxia and marched into the Mian region.

sentences.zh: 稱將二百人下見亮，亮素惡稱輕狡，數稱前後罪惡，收而斬之。

translations.literal: Cheng brought two hundred men down to see Liang; Liang had long hated Cheng for frivolity and cunning, recounted Cheng's past crimes one after another, seized him, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Cheng came downriver with two hundred men to pay his respects to Yu Liang. Liang had long despised him for his frivolity and deceit; he listed Cheng's past crimes and had him seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 後以魏興險遠，命庾懌徙屯半洲；

translations.literal: Later, because Weixing was perilous and remote, Yu Liang was ordered to move his camp to Banzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Weixing was remote and hard to defend, Yu Yi was ordered to move his camp to Banzhou;

sentences.zh: 更以武昌太守陳囂為梁州刺史，趣漢中。

translations.literal: Chen Xi, Administrator of Wuchang, was made Inspector of Liang Province in his stead and hurried to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xi, Administrator of Wuchang, was appointed Inspector of Liang Province in his place and sent to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍李松攻漢巴郡、江陽。

translations.literal: He dispatched Staff Officer Li Song to attack Han's Ba Commandery and Jiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Staff Officer Li Song to attack Ba Commandery and Jiangyang in Han.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，執漢荊州刺史李閎、巴郡太守黃植送建康。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Han's Inspector of Jing Province Li Hong and Prefect of Ba Commandery Huang Zhi were seized and sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Li Hong, Inspector of Jing Province in Han, and Huang Zhi, Prefect of Ba Commandery, were captured and sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 漢主壽以李弈為鎮東將軍，代閎守巴郡。

translations.literal: Han's ruler Shou made Li Yi Eastern Garrison General to replace Hong and guard Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shou of Han appointed Li Yi Eastern Garrison General to replace Hong and hold Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 庾亮上疏言：「蜀甚弱而胡尚強，欲帥大眾十萬移鎮石城，遣諸軍羅布江、沔為伐趙之規。」

translations.literal: Yu Liang submitted a memorial saying, "Shu is very weak while the barbarians are still strong; I wish to lead a great host of one hundred thousand and move my headquarters to Stone City, dispatching the armies to spread out along the Yangzi and Mian as a plan to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang submitted a memorial: "Shu is weak and the barbarians still strong. I propose to move my headquarters to Stone City at the head of a hundred thousand men and deploy our forces along the Yangzi and Mian as the opening move against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 帝下其議。

translations.literal: The emperor submitted it for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the proposal to the court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 丞相導請許之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Wang Dao requested that it be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wang Dao urged approval.

sentences.zh: 大尉鑒議，以為：「資用未備，不可大舉。」

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Xi Jian deliberated and held that "the resources are not yet prepared; a great campaign cannot be launched."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xi Jian argued that "our supplies are not yet in place; we cannot launch a major campaign."

sentences.zh: 太常蔡謨議，以為：「時有否泰，道有屈伸，苟不計強弱而輕動，則亡不終日，何功之有！
