translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Cai Mo deliberated and held that "there are times of adversity and prosperity; the Way has its bending and straightening—if one does not reckon strength and weakness and acts rashly, destruction will come within the day; what achievement could there be!
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Cai Mo argued: "Fortune rises and falls; the Way advances and retreats. To move rashly without weighing strength against weakness is to invite ruin within a day. What victory could come of that?

sentences.zh: 為今之計，莫若養威以俟時。

translations.literal: The plan for the present is none better than nurturing prestige and awaiting the time.
translations.idiomatic: The wise course now is to build our strength and wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 時之可否系胡之強弱，胡之強弱系石虎之能否。

translations.literal: Whether the time is favorable depends on the barbarians' strength or weakness; the barbarians' strength or weakness depends on whether Shi Hu is capable.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the moment is ripe depends on how strong the barbarians are, and their strength depends on whether Shi Hu is truly capable.

sentences.zh: 自石勒舉事，虎常為爪牙，百戰百勝，遂定中原，所據之地，同於魏世。

translations.literal: From the time Shi Le raised his enterprise, Hu was always his claws and teeth; in a hundred battles he won a hundred victories and thereby settled the Central Plains; the territory he held was the same as in Wei times.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Shi Le rose to power, Shi Hu was his right hand—victorious in a hundred battles, he secured the Central Plains and held territory equal to what Wei had once ruled.

sentences.zh: 勒死之後，虎挾嗣君，誅將相；

translations.literal: After Le's death Hu controlled the young ruler and executed generals and ministers;
translations.idiomatic: After Le's death Shi Hu seized control of the young emperor and purged generals and ministers;

sentences.zh: 內難既平，剪削外寇，一舉而拔金墉，再戰而擒石生，誅石聰如拾遺，取郭權如振槁，四境之內，不失尺土。

translations.literal: once internal troubles were settled he cut down external foes—in one move he took Jinyong, in a second battle he captured Shi Sheng; he executed Shi Cong as easily as picking up something dropped, took Guo Quan as easily as shaking dry stalks; within the four borders not a foot of land was lost.
translations.idiomatic: once internal threats were crushed he turned on external enemies—taking Jinyong in one stroke, capturing Shi Sheng in a second battle, executing Shi Cong as easily as picking up a dropped object, and seizing Guo Quan as easily as snapping a dry twig, all without losing an inch of territory.

sentences.zh: 以是觀之，虎為能乎，將不能也？

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, is Hu capable, or is he not?
translations.idiomatic: Judging by this record, is Shi Hu capable—or is he not?

sentences.zh: 論者以胡前攻襄陽不能拔，謂之無能為。

translations.literal: Discussants, because the barbarians formerly attacked Xiangyang and could not take it, call him incapable.
translations.idiomatic: Some call him incapable because the barbarians once failed to capture Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 夫百戰百勝之強而以不拔一城為劣，譬諸射擊百發百中而一失，可以謂之拙乎？

translations.literal: A power that wins a hundred battles in a hundred and is judged inferior for not taking one city—is that like calling an archer clumsy who hits the mark a hundred times and misses once?
translations.idiomatic: To call a commander who has won a hundred battles in a hundred inferior because he failed to take one city—is that like calling an archer a poor shot because he missed once after a hundred bullseyes?

sentences.zh: 「且石遇，偏師也，桓平北，邊將也，所爭者疆場之土，利則進，否則退，非所急也。

translations.literal: Moreover Shi Yu was a detached column, and Huan the Pacifier of the North was a frontier general; what they contested was borderland soil—if there was profit they advanced, if not they withdrew; it was not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Shi Yu commanded only a detached column, and Huan the Pacifier of the North was a frontier general. They fought over border territory—advancing when gain was possible, withdrawing when it was not. That was no decisive contest.

sentences.zh: 今征西以重鎮名賢，自將大軍欲席捲河南，虎必自帥一國之眾來決勝負，豈得以襄陽為比哉！

translations.literal: Now the Western Campaigning General, a man of great reputation holding a key post, personally leads a great army wishing to sweep through Henan; Hu is certain to lead the host of an entire state to decide victory and defeat—how can this be compared with Xiangyang!
translations.idiomatic: Now Yu Liang, a celebrated commander holding a vital post, proposes to lead a great army and sweep through Henan. Shi Hu will surely march out with the full strength of his state to decide the issue—how can that be compared with the fight for Xiangyang?

sentences.zh: 今征西欲與之戰，何如石生？

translations.literal: If the Western Campaigning General wishes to give battle, how does he compare with Shi Sheng?
translations.idiomatic: If Yu Liang means to fight in the open field, how does he measure against Shi Sheng?

sentences.zh: 若欲城守，何如金墉？

translations.literal: If he wishes to hold walled cities, how does he compare with Jinyong?
translations.idiomatic: If he means to hold walled cities, how do his defenses compare with Jinyong?

sentences.zh: 欲阻沔水，何如大江？

translations.literal: If he wishes to block the Mian River, how does it compare with the Great River?
translations.idiomatic: If he means to block the Mian, how does that barrier compare with the Yangzi?

sentences.zh: 欲拒石虎，何如蘇峻？

translations.literal: If he wishes to resist Shi Hu, how does he compare with Su Jun?
translations.idiomatic: If he means to stand against Shi Hu, how does he compare with Su Jun?

sentences.zh: 凡此數者，宜詳校之。

translations.literal: Each of these several points ought to be weighed carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Each of these comparisons deserves careful reckoning.

sentences.zh: 「石生猛將，關中精兵，征西之戰殆不能勝也。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng was a fierce general with the elite troops of Guanzhong; in battle with the Western Campaigning General he would probably not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng was a fierce commander with Guanzhong's finest troops; Yu Liang would probably not defeat him in battle.

sentences.zh: 金墉險固，劉曜十萬眾不能拔，征西之守殆不能勝也。

translations.literal: Jinyong was perilous and strong; Liu Yao with a hundred thousand men could not take it—the Western Campaigning General's defense would probably not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyong was formidable; Liu Yao with a hundred thousand men could not take it—Yu Liang's defenses would probably fare no better.

sentences.zh: 又當是時，洛陽、關中皆舉兵擊虎，今此三鎮反為其用；

translations.literal: Moreover at that time Luoyang and Guanzhong both raised troops to strike Hu; now these three garrisons instead serve him;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in those days Luoyang and Guanzhong both rose against Shi Hu; now these three garrisons would fight for him instead;

sentences.zh: 方之於前，倍半之勢也。

translations.literal: compared with before, the advantage is one and a half times as great.
translations.idiomatic: compared with then, his position is half again as strong.

sentences.zh: 石生不能敵其半，而征西欲當其倍，愚所疑也。

translations.literal: Shi Sheng could not withstand even half of him, yet the Western Campaigning General wishes to meet his double—I am doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Sheng could not withstand even half Shi Hu's strength, yet Yu Liang proposes to meet double that force—I have my doubts.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之強不及石虎，沔水之險不及大江；

translations.literal: Su Jun's strength did not match Shi Hu's, and the peril of the Mian River did not match the Great River;
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun was not as strong as Shi Hu, and the Mian was not as formidable a barrier as the Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 大江不能御蘇峻，而欲以沔水御石虎，又所疑也。

translations.literal: the Great River could not hold back Su Jun, yet one wishes to use the Mian River to hold back Shi Hu—again I am doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: the Yangzi could not stop Su Jun, yet we would rely on the Mian to stop Shi Hu—I doubt that too.

sentences.zh: 昔祖士稚在譙，佃於城北界，胡來攻，豫置軍屯以御其外。

translations.literal: Formerly Zu Ti at Qiao farmed on the northern border of the city; when the barbarians came to attack he pre-positioned army camps outside to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zu Ti at Qiao farmed on the city's northern outskirts. When the barbarians attacked, he had camps stationed outside to meet them.

sentences.zh: 谷將熟，胡果至，丁夫戰於外，老弱獲於內，多持炬火，急則燒谷而走。

translations.literal: When the grain was nearly ripe the barbarians indeed arrived; fighting men battled outside while the old and weak harvested within, many carrying torches—if pressed they burned the grain and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain was nearly ripe the barbarians came. Fighting men battled outside while the old and weak harvested within, many carrying torches ready to burn the crop and flee if pressed.

sentences.zh: 如此數年，竟不得其利。

translations.literal: In this way for several years he ultimately obtained no profit.
translations.idiomatic: For years he gained nothing by it.

sentences.zh: 當是時，胡唯據河北，方之於今，四分之一耳；

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians held only north of the Yellow River; compared with today it was but one quarter;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the barbarians held only the territory north of the Yellow River—a quarter of what they hold today;

sentences.zh: 士稚不能捍其一，而征西欲以御其四，又所疑也。

translations.literal: Zu Ti could not hold back even one part of them, yet the Western Campaigning General wishes to hold back four parts—I am again doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti could not hold back even a quarter of their strength, yet Yu Liang proposes to hold back the whole—I doubt that as well.

sentences.zh: 「然此但論征西既至之後耳，尚未論道路之慮也。

translations.literal: Yet this discusses only after the Western Campaigning General has arrived; the difficulties of the road have not yet been discussed.
translations.idiomatic: And this addresses only what happens after Yu Liang arrives—it does not yet consider the hazards of the march itself.

sentences.zh: 自沔以西，水急岸高，魚貫溯流，首尾百里。

translations.literal: From west of the Mian the water is swift and the banks high; the troops must file upstream in a single line, head to tail for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Mian the current runs fast and the banks rise steep. An army must file upstream in single column, stretching head to tail for a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 若胡無宋襄之義，及我未陣而擊之，將若之何？

translations.literal: If the barbarians lack the righteousness of Duke Xiang of Song and strike before we have formed ranks, what then?
translations.idiomatic: If the barbarians show no scruples like Duke Xiang of Song and attack before we can form ranks, what then?

sentences.zh: 今王土與胡，水陸異勢，便習不同；

translations.literal: Now our realm and the barbarians differ in advantage on water and land, and in what they are practiced at;
translations.idiomatic: Our realm and the barbarians differ in their advantages on land and water and in what each is trained for;

sentences.zh: 胡若送死，則敵之有餘，若棄江遠進，以我所短擊彼所長，懼非廟勝之算也。」

translations.literal: if the barbarians come to die fighting, the enemy will have the surplus; if we abandon the river and advance far, using our shortcoming to strike their strength—I fear this is not a plan calculated to victory in the temple."
translations.idiomatic: if they come ready to die fighting, the advantage is theirs; if we leave the river and march deep inland, pitting our weakness against their strength—I fear that is no strategy the court should approve."

sentences.zh: 朝議多與謨同。

translations.literal: The court deliberation largely agreed with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Most at court sided with Cai Mo.

sentences.zh: 乃詔亮不聽移鎮。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued that Liang was not permitted to move his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The court then decreed that Yu Liang would not be allowed to relocate his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 燕前軍師慕容評、廣威將軍慕容軍、折衝將軍慕輿根、蕩寇將軍慕輿泥襲趙遼西，俘獲千餘家而去。

translations.literal: Former Chief Strategist of Yan Murong Ping, General of Broad Prestige Murong Jun, General Who Breaks the Foe Murong Gen, and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits Murong Ni raided Liaoxi in Zhao, captured more than a thousand households, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping, former Chief Strategist of Yan, together with Generals Murong Jun, Murong Gen, and Murong Ni, raided Liaoxi in Zhao, captured more than a thousand households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 趙鎮遠將軍石成、積弩將軍呼延晃、建威將軍張支等追之，評等與戰，斬晃、支首。

translations.literal: Zhao's Distant Garrison General Shi Cheng, Strong Crossbow General Huyan Huang, Establishing Prestige General Zhang Zhi, and others pursued them; Ping and the others gave battle and beheaded Huang and Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cheng, Distant Garrison General of Zhao, Huyan Huang, Strong Crossbow General, Zhang Zhi, Establishing Prestige General, and others gave chase. Murong Ping and his men fought them and beheaded Huang and Zhi.

sentences.zh: 段遼謀反於燕，燕人殺遼及其黨與數十人，送遼首於趙。

translations.literal: Duan Liao plotted rebellion in Yan; the people of Yan killed Liao and several tens of his partisans and sent Liao's head to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Liao plotted rebellion against Yan. The Yan court killed him and several dozen of his followers and sent his head to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 五月，代王什翼犍會諸大人於參合陂，議都灅源川。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Prince of Dai Shiyijian convened the tribal elders at Canhe Marsh and deliberated on making the capital at Shuiyuan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince Tuoba Shiyijian gathered the tribal elders at Canhe Marsh to discuss establishing the capital on the Shuiyuan River.

sentences.zh: 其母王氏曰：「吾自先世以來，以遷徙為業。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Wang said, "From our forebears onward we have made our living by moving from place to place.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Wang, said, "Since the time of our ancestors we have lived by wandering from place to place.

sentences.zh: 今國家多難，若城郭而居，一旦寇來，無所避之。」

translations.literal: Now the state faces many troubles; if we settle behind walls, once invaders come there will be nowhere to flee."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is beset with troubles. If we build a walled city and settle in it, when raiders come we shall have nowhere to run.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: So he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With that she persuaded him, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 代人謂它國之民來附者皆為烏桓，什翼犍分之為二部，各置大人以監之。

translations.literal: The people of Dai called all subjects from other states who came to submit Wuhuan; Shiyijian divided them into two divisions, placing a tribal chief over each to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai people applied the name Wuhuan to all subjects from other states who came over to them. Shiyijian split them into two divisions and appointed a tribal chief to supervise each.

sentences.zh: 弟孤監其北，子寔君監其南。

translations.literal: Younger brother Gu oversaw the north; his son Shijun oversaw the south.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Gu supervised the northern division, and his son Shijun the southern.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍求昏於燕，燕王皝以其妹妻之。

translations.literal: Shiyijian sought marriage with Yan; King Murong Huang gave him his younger sister as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian asked for a marriage alliance with Yan, and King Murong Huang gave him his younger sister in marriage.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，趙王虎以太子宣為大單于，建天子旌旗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhao King Shi Hu made Crown Prince Xuan Grand Chanyu and established the banners and flags of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhao King Shi Hu appointed Crown Prince Xuan Grand Chanyu and set up the imperial banners and standards.

sentences.zh: 庚申，始興文獻公王導薨，喪葬之禮視漢博陸候及安平獻王故事，參用天子之禮。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wang Dao, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, died; the funeral rites followed the precedents of the Marquis of Bolu and the King Xian of Ping'an of Han, with parts of the Son of Heaven's rites incorporated.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Wang Dao, Duke Wenxian of Shixing, died. His funeral followed the precedents set for Huo Guang, Marquis of Bolu, and Liu Fu, King Xian of Ping'an, with elements of an emperor's rites mixed in.

sentences.zh: 導簡素寡慾，善因事就功，雖無日用之益而歲計有餘。

translations.literal: Dao was plain and frugal with few desires; he was skilled at achieving success by adapting to circumstances; though there was no benefit for daily use, the yearly reckoning still showed surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Dao lived plainly and frugally, with few wants. He knew how to turn events to advantage, and though day-to-day gains were modest, the year's accounts always showed a surplus.

sentences.zh: 輔相三世，倉無儲谷，衣不重帛。

translations.literal: Having served as chief minister through three reigns, the granary held no stored grain and his garments did not layer silk.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as chief minister through three reigns, his granary held no reserve grain and he never wore more than one layer of silk.

sentences.zh: 初，導與庾亮共薦丹楊尹何充於帝，請以為己副，且曰：「臣死之日，願引充內侍，則社稷無虞矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Dao together with Yu Liang jointly recommended Dan Yang Intendant He Chong to the emperor, asking that he be made his deputy, and said, "On the day this minister dies, I wish that Chong be brought in to attend within, then the altars of state will be without worry."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dao and Yu Liang had jointly recommended Dan Yang Intendant He Chong to the emperor and asked that he be made Dao's deputy, saying, "When I die, I hope Chong may be brought in to serve at court; then the altars of state will be secure.

sentences.zh: 由是加吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Accordingly he was additionally made Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: On that recommendation Chong was also appointed Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 及導薨，微庾亮為丞相、揚州刺史、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: When Dao died, Yu Liang was summoned to be Chief Minister, Inspector of Yang Province, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: After Dao's death the court summoned Yu Liang to serve as Chief Minister, Inspector of Yang Province, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 亮固辭。

translations.literal: Liang firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liang steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以充為護軍將軍，亮弟會稽內史冰為中書監、揚州刺史，參錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Chong was made General Who Protects the Army; Liang's younger brother Bing, Interior Minister of Kuaiji, was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province, participating in recording affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou He Chong was appointed General Who Protects the Army, and Liang's younger brother Bing, Interior Minister of Kuaiji, was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province, with a share in recording the Masters of Writing's affairs.

sentences.zh: 冰既當重任，經綸時務，不捨晝夜，賓禮朝賢，升擢後進，由是朝野翕然稱之，以為賢相。

translations.literal: Once Bing took on heavy responsibility, he arranged current affairs without cease day or night, receiving guests with courtesy toward court worthies and promoting the junior, whereupon court and countryside uniformly praised him, considering him a worthy chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bing assumed heavy responsibilities, he managed state affairs day and night without rest, treating court worthies with courtesy and advancing younger talent. Court and countryside alike praised him as a worthy chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，王導輔政，每從寬恕；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Dao assisted in governance, he always inclined toward leniency;
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, when Wang Dao governed, he always leaned toward clemency;

sentences.zh: 冰頗任威刑，丹楊尹殷融諫之。

translations.literal: Bing relied rather on imposing punishments; Dan Yang Intendant Yin Rong remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Bing leaned instead on harsh punishments, and Dan Yang Intendant Yin Rong remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 冰曰：「前相之賢，猶不堪其弘，況如吾者哉！」

translations.literal: Bing said, "The former chief minister's worthiness could still not bear his magnanimity—how much less one like me!"
translations.idiomatic: Bing said, "Even our former chief minister, for all his talent, could not sustain such broad leniency—how much less can someone like me!

sentences.zh: 范汪謂冰曰：「頃天文錯度，足下宜盡消御之道。」

translations.literal: Fan Wang said to Bing, "Recently the stars have gone out of their measures; Your Excellency ought fully to practice the way of dispelling and guarding against this."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wang then told Bing, "The heavens have lately shown ominous signs. You should do everything you can to ward them off.

sentences.zh: 冰曰：「玄象豈吾所測，正當勤盡人事耳。」

translations.literal: Bing said, "Can the dark signs be something I can measure? One should simply strive to fulfill human affairs, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Bing replied, "How can I read the heavens? All one can do is work diligently at human affairs.

sentences.zh: 又隱實戶口，料出無名萬餘人，以充軍實。

translations.literal: He also concealed and verified household registers, reckoning out more than ten thousand nameless persons to fill out military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He also conducted a hidden census and uncovered more than ten thousand unregistered persons to bolster the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 冰好為糾察，近於繁細，後益矯違，復存寬縱，疏密自由，律令無用矣。

translations.literal: Bing loved to conduct investigations, approaching excessive detail; later he increasingly overcorrected in violation, again preserving leniency and indulgence—the strict and the loose at his own discretion, and the laws and orders were of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Bing loved to pry into affairs to the point of fussy detail. Later he swung to the opposite extreme and relapsed into laxity, tightening or loosening as he pleased until law and regulation ceased to matter.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬午，復改丞相為司徒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renwu, the title of Chief Minister was again changed to Excellency over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renwu, the office of Chief Minister was again renamed Excellency over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 南昌文成公郗鑒疾篤，以府事付長史劉遐，上疏乞骸骨，且曰：「臣所統錯雜，率多北人，或逼遷徙，或是新附，百姓懷土，皆有歸本之心；

translations.literal: Xi Jian, Duke Wencheng of Nanchang, was gravely ill; he entrusted office matters to Chief Clerk Liu Xia, submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and said, "The people under this minister's command are mixed and tangled, mostly northerners—some forcibly relocated, some newly submitted; the common people cherish their native soil and all have hearts to return to their roots;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian, Duke Wencheng of Nanchang, fell gravely ill. He handed office affairs to Chief Clerk Liu Xia and submitted a memorial asking to retire, writing, "The people under my command are a tangled mix, mostly northerners—some forcibly moved south, some newly submitted. They cherish their native land and all long to return home;

sentences.zh: 臣宣國恩，示以好惡，處與田宅，漸得少安。

translations.literal: this minister has proclaimed the state's grace, shown good and ill, provided dwellings and fields, and they have gradually attained a measure of peace.
translations.idiomatic: I have proclaimed the state's kindness, shown them reward and punishment, and given them homes and fields, and they have gradually found a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 聞臣疾篤，眾情駭動，若當北渡，必啟寇心。

translations.literal: Hearing that this minister's illness is grave, public sentiment is shaken with alarm; if they should cross north, it will surely awaken the invaders' ambition.
translations.idiomatic: If they hear that I am dying, the people will panic. Should they try to flee north, that will surely stir the enemy's appetite for invasion.

sentences.zh: 太常臣謨，平簡貞正，素望所歸，謂可以為都督、徐州刺史。」

translations.literal: Your subject Mo, Minister of Ceremonies, is even, simple, upright, and honest—the reputation to which all look; I hold that he can serve as area commander and Inspector of Xu Province."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Cai Mo is steady, plain, and upright, and enjoys the trust of all. I believe he can serve as area commander and Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 詔以蔡謨為太尉軍司，加侍中、辛酉，鑒薨，即以謨為征北將軍、都督徐、兗、青三州諸軍事、徐州刺史，假節。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cai Mo as army aide to the Grand Commandant and additionally Palace Attendant. On xinyou, Xi Jian died, and Mo was immediately made General Who Campaigns North, area commander over the military affairs of Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces, Inspector of Xu Province, with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Cai Mo army aide to the Grand Commandant and additionally Palace Attendant. On xinyou Xi Jian died, and Mo was at once made General Who Campaigns North, area commander over Xu, Yan, and Qing, Inspector of Xu Province, with full military authority.

sentences.zh: 時左衛將軍陳光請伐趙，詔遣光攻壽陽。

translations.literal: At the time Left Guard General Chen Guang requested a campaign against Zhao; an edict dispatched Guang to attack Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Guard General Chen Guang asked to campaign against Zhao, and the court ordered him to attack Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 謨上疏曰：「壽陽城小而固。

translations.literal: Mo submitted a memorial saying, "Shouyang's walls are small but strong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo submitted a memorial: "Shouyang is small but strongly fortified.

sentences.zh: 自壽陽至琅邪，城壁相望，一城見攻，眾城必救。

translations.literal: From Shouyang to Langye, city walls face one another; if one city is attacked, the crowd of cities will surely come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: From Shouyang to Langye the fortresses stand in sight of one another; attack one and the rest will rush to its relief.

sentences.zh: 又，王師在路五十餘日，前驅未至，聲息久聞，賊之郵驛，一日千里，河北之騎，足以來赴。

translations.literal: Moreover, the royal army has been on the road more than fifty days; the vanguard has not arrived and news of our approach has long been heard—the invaders' courier stations cover a thousand li in a day, and the cavalry north of the Yellow River are sufficient to come to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Our army has already been on the march for more than fifty days. The vanguard has not yet arrived, yet the enemy has long since heard of us. Their couriers can cover a thousand li in a day, and the cavalry north of the Yellow River can reach Shouyang in time.

sentences.zh: 夫以白起、韓信、項籍之勇，猶發梁焚舟，背水而陣。

translations.literal: Even men of the courage of Bai Qi, Han Xin, and Xiang Ji still dismantled bridges and burned boats, making their stand with water at their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Even commanders as bold as Bai Qi, Han Xin, and Xiang Yu burned their boats and fought with their backs to the water.

sentences.zh: 今欲停船水渚，引兵造城，前對堅敵，顧臨歸路，此兵法之所誡。

translations.literal: Now to moor boats at the water's edge and lead troops to the city, facing hardened foes in front while looking back on the road home—this is what military treatises warn against.
translations.idiomatic: To anchor our ships and march on the city with a strong enemy ahead and our retreat behind us is exactly what the military classics forbid.

sentences.zh: 若進攻未拔，胡騎猝至，懼桓子不知所為而舟中之指可掬也。

translations.literal: If the assault is not taken and barbarian cavalry arrive suddenly, I fear Huan Zi would not know what to do and the fingers on the boat could be scooped up.
translations.idiomatic: If the assault fails and barbarian horsemen arrive suddenly, I fear panic will spread through the ranks—as when, in the old story, the men on the boat clawed one another in terror.

sentences.zh: 今光所將皆殿中精兵，宜令所向有征無戰。

translations.literal: Those Guang now leads are all elite troops of the palace guard; they should be made so that wherever they go there is conquest without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The men Chen Guang commands are the palace guard's finest; they should be used where they can conquer without a fight.

sentences.zh: 而頓之堅城之下，以國之爪士擊寇之下邑，得之則利薄而不足損敵，失之則害重而足以益寇，懼非策之長者也。」

translations.literal: Yet to halt them beneath stout walls and use the state's foremost warriors to strike the invaders' lesser city—if taken the gain is slight and insufficient to harm the foe; if lost the harm is grave and enough to strengthen the invaders. I fear this is not the better part of strategy."
translations.idiomatic: To keep them stalled before a strong wall, sending the empire's best soldiers against an enemy outpost, would yield little if we win and cost dearly if we lose—strengthening the foe rather than weakening him. I do not think this is sound strategy.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: So the campaign was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his advice and called off the attack.

sentences.zh: 初，陶侃在武昌，議者以江北有邾城，宜分兵戍之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tao Kan was at Wuchang, deliberators held that on the north bank there was Zhu City and troops ought to be divided to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Kan held Wuchang, some argued that Zhu City on the north bank ought to be garrisoned with a separate force.

sentences.zh: 侃每不答，而言者不巳。

translations.literal: Kan each time made no reply, but those who spoke did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Kan each time said nothing, but the advocates would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 侃乃渡水獵，引將佐語之曰：「我所以設險而禦寇者，正以長江耳。

translations.literal: Kan then crossed the water to hunt and, gathering his generals and aides, said to them, "The reason I set defenses to repel invaders is precisely the Yangzi alone.
translations.idiomatic: Kan then crossed the river on a hunting trip and, gathering his officers, told them, "I rely on the Yangzi alone to keep invaders out.

sentences.zh: 邾城隔在江北，內無所倚，外接群夷。

translations.literal: Zhu City stands separated north of the river, with nothing within to lean on and outward contact with the manifold tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu City lies north of the river with no support behind it and open contact with the tribal peoples beyond.

sentences.zh: 夷中利深，晉人貪利，夷不堪命，必引虜入寇。

translations.literal: Deep profit lies among the tribes; Jin men are greedy for profit and the tribes cannot bear the demands—they will surely lead the barbarians in to raid.
translations.idiomatic: There is rich profit to be had among the tribes. Jin men will greedily exploit them until the tribes can bear no more and invite the barbarians in to raid.

sentences.zh: 此乃致禍之由，非禦寇也。

translations.literal: This is the source that brings calamity, not a means of repelling invaders.
translations.idiomatic: That would invite disaster, not repel invasion.

sentences.zh: 且吳時戍此城，用三萬兵，今縱有兵守之，亦無益於江南；

translations.literal: Moreover when Wu garrisoned this city they used thirty thousand troops; even if troops were stationed there now, it would also be of no benefit to the lands south of the river;
translations.idiomatic: When Wu held the city it took thirty thousand men to garrison it. Even if we posted troops there now, they would do the south no good;

sentences.zh: 若羯虜有可乘之會，此又非所資也。」

translations.literal: if the Jie barbarians had an opportunity that could be seized, this would again not be something to rely upon."
translations.idiomatic: and if the Jie barbarians saw a chance to strike, the garrison would be no help at all."

sentences.zh: 及庾亮鎮武昌，卒使毛寶、樊峻戍邾城。

translations.literal: When Yu Liang held Wuchang, he finally made Mao Bao and Fan Jun garrison Zhu City.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Liang took command at Wuchang, he sent Mao Bao and Fan Jun to garrison Zhu City after all.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎惡之，以夔安為大都督，帥石鑒、石閔、李農、張貉、李菟等五將軍、兵五萬人寇荊、揚北鄙，二萬騎攻邾城。

translations.literal: Zhao King Shi Hu hated this; he made Kui An Grand Commander-in-Chief, leading five generals—Shi Jian, Shi Min, Li Nong, Zhang He, and Li Tu—and fifty thousand troops to raid the northern borders of Jing and Yang, while twenty thousand horsemen attacked Zhu City.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao King Shi Hu resented the garrison. He appointed Kui An Grand Commander-in-Chief and sent him with five generals—Shi Jian, Shi Min, Li Nong, Zhang He, and Li Tu—and fifty thousand men to raid the northern marches of Jing and Yang, while twenty thousand cavalry struck Zhu City.

sentences.zh: 毛寶求救於庾亮，亮以城固，不時遣兵。

translations.literal: Mao Bao asked Yu Liang for rescue; Liang because the city was strong did not timely dispatch troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Bao begged Yu Liang for relief, but Liang, believing the city could hold, delayed sending help.

sentences.zh: 九月，石閔敗晉兵於沔陰，殺將軍蔡懷；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Shi Min defeated Jin troops at Mianyin and killed General Cai Huai;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shi Min routed Jin forces at Mianyin and killed General Cai Huai;

sentences.zh: 夔安、李農陷沔南；

translations.literal: Kui An and Li Nong took Miannan;
translations.idiomatic: Kui An and Li Nong captured the south bank of the Mian;

sentences.zh: 朱保敗晉兵於白石，殺鄭豹等五將軍；

translations.literal: Zhu Bao defeated Jin troops at Baishi and killed five generals including Zheng Bao;
translations.idiomatic: At Baishi Zhu Bao routed the Jin army and slew five generals, among them Zheng Bao;

sentences.zh: 張貉陷邾城，死者六千人，毛寶、樊峻突圍出走，赴江溺死。

translations.literal: Zhang He took Zhu City—six thousand dead; Mao Bao and Fan Jun broke out and fled, rushed into the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He captured Zhu City at a cost of six thousand lives. Mao Bao and Fan Jun broke out, fled to the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 夔安進據胡亭，寇江夏；

translations.literal: Kui An advanced and occupied Hu Pavilion and raided Jiangxia;
translations.idiomatic: Kui An pushed forward, seized Hu Pavilion, and raided Jiangxia;

sentences.zh: 義陽將軍黃沖、義陽太守鄭進皆降於趙。

translations.literal: General of Righteousness Huang Chong and Prefect of Righteousness Zheng Jin both surrendered to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chong, General of Righteousness, and Zheng Jin, Prefect of Righteousness, both went over to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 安進圍石城，竟陵太守李陽拒戰，破之，斬首五千餘級，安乃退。

translations.literal: An advanced to besiege Stone City; Prefect of Jingling Li Yang resisted in battle, defeated them, and beheaded more than five thousand; An then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Kui An went on to besiege Shicheng, but Jingling Prefect Li Yang fought him off, killed more than five thousand of his men, and forced him to retreat.

sentences.zh: 遂掠漢東，擁七千餘戶遷於幽、冀。

translations.literal: He then plundered east of the Han and relocated more than seven thousand households to You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao army then ravaged the Han River region and relocated more than seven thousand households to You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 是時，庾亮猶上疏欲遷鎮石城，聞邾城陷。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang still submitted a memorial wishing to move his headquarters to Stone City; he heard that Zhu City had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang was still petitioning to move his headquarters to Stone City when he learned that Zhu City had fallen.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 上表陳謝，自貶三等，行安西將軍；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial of confession and self-reproach, demoting himself three ranks and acting as General Who Pacifies the West;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial of apology, stripped himself of three ranks, and served temporarily as General Who Pacifies the West;

sentences.zh: 有詔復位。

translations.literal: an edict restored his rank.
translations.idiomatic: the court issued an edict restoring his former rank.

sentences.zh: 以輔國將軍庾懌為豫州刺史，監宣城、廬江、歷陽、安豐四郡諸軍事，假節，鎮蕪湖。

translations.literal: Assistant General Yu Yi was made Inspector of Yu Province, overseeing military affairs of the four commanderies Xuancheng, Lujiang, Liyang, and Anfeng, with credential staff, garrisoning Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant General Yu Yi was appointed Inspector of Yu Province, with authority over Xuancheng, Lujiang, Liyang, and Anfeng, and was posted at Wuhu with full military credentials.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎患貴戚豪恣，乃擢殿中御史李巨為御史中丞，特加親任，中外肅然。

translations.literal: Zhao King Shi Hu was troubled by the arrogance of noble kin and great families; he promoted Palace Censor Li Ju to Censor-in-Chief, granting special personal trust, and within and without the court all were awed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao King Shi Hu worried about the arrogance of the imperial clan and great families. He promoted Palace Censor Li Ju to Censor-in-Chief and gave him unusual personal trust, and the whole court, inside and out, fell into awe.

sentences.zh: 虎曰：「朕聞良臣如猛虎，高步曠野而豺狼避路，信哉！」

translations.literal: Hu said, "We have heard that a good minister is like a fierce tiger—striding the open wild while jackals and wolves avoid the path—how true!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu said, "They say a worthy minister is like a fierce tiger walking the open wild while jackals and wolves slink from the path. How true that is!"

sentences.zh: 虎以撫軍將軍李農為使持節、監遼西、北平諸軍事、征東將軍、營州牧，鎮令支。

translations.literal: Hu made General of the Pacifying Army Li Nong bearer of staff with full powers, overseer of military affairs of Liaoxi and Beiping, General Who Campaigns East, Regional Governor of Ying Province, garrisoning Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu appointed General of the Pacifying Army Li Nong full commissioner, overseer of military affairs in Liaoxi and Beiping, General Who Campaigns East, and Regional Governor of Ying Province, with his headquarters at Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 農帥眾三萬與征北大將軍張舉攻燕凡城。

translations.literal: Nong led a host of thirty thousand together with Grand General Who Campaigns North Zhang Ju to attack Fan City in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong led thirty thousand men together with Grand General Who Campaigns North Zhang Ju to attack Fan City in Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝以榼盧城大悅綰為御難將軍，授兵一千，使守凡城。

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Huang made Dayue Guan of Kelu City General Who Meets Hardship, gave him a thousand troops, and sent him to hold Fan City.
translations.idiomatic: Yan King Murong Huang appointed Dayue Guan of Kelu City General Who Meets Hardship, gave him a thousand men, and ordered him to hold Fan City.

sentences.zh: 及趙兵至，將吏皆恐，欲棄城走。

translations.literal: When Zhao troops arrived, generals and officials were all afraid and wished to abandon the city and flee.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhao army arrived, the officers all feared for their lives and wanted to abandon the city and flee.

sentences.zh: 綰曰：「受命禦寇，死生以之。

translations.literal: Guan said, "Having received orders to repel invaders, life and death follow from this.
translations.idiomatic: Guan said, "We were ordered to hold against the enemy. Our lives are bound to this duty.

sentences.zh: 且憑城堅守，一可敵百，有敢妄言惑眾者斬！」

translations.literal: Moreover, relying on stout walls to hold firm, one can match a hundred; whoever dares speak reckless words to unsettle the masses—behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: Behind these walls one man can hold off a hundred. Anyone who spreads panic will be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 眾然後定。

translations.literal: The crowd then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the troops steady themselves.

sentences.zh: 綰身先士卒，親冒矢石；

translations.literal: Guan himself went before the soldiers and personally braved arrows and stones;
translations.idiomatic: Guan himself took the lead, exposing himself to arrows and stones;

sentences.zh: 舉等攻之經旬，不能克，乃退。

translations.literal: Ju and the others assaulted for ten-odd days and could not take it, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju and his forces besieged the city for more than ten days without success and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 虎以遼西迫近燕境，數遭攻襲，乃悉徙其民於冀州之南。

translations.literal: Hu because Liaoxi pressed close on Yan's borders and repeatedly suffered attacks and raids, then entirely relocated its people south of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liaoxi lay on Yan's border and suffered repeated raids, Shi Hu moved its entire population south of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 漢主壽疾病，羅恆、解思明復議奉晉；

translations.literal: Han's ruler Shou was ill; Luo Heng and Jie Siming again deliberated on submitting to Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Shou fell ill, and Luo Heng and Jie Siming again urged submitting to Jin;

sentences.zh: 壽不從。

translations.literal: Shou did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shou refused.

sentences.zh: 李演復上書言之；

translations.literal: Li Yan again submitted a memorial stating this;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan again memorialized the throne on the same point;

sentences.zh: 壽怒，殺演。

translations.literal: Shou in anger killed Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had him executed in a rage.

sentences.zh: 壽常慕漢武、魏明之為人，恥聞父兄時事，上書者不得言先世政教，自以為勝之也。

translations.literal: Shou often admired the conduct of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Wei; he was ashamed to hear of his father and elder brother's times—memorialists were not permitted to speak of earlier generations' governance and teaching; he considered himself to surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Shou admired the example of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Wei and was ashamed to hear talk of his father's and elder brother's reigns. Memorialists were forbidden to mention the policies of earlier rulers; he believed himself their superior.

sentences.zh: 舍人杜襲作詩十篇，託言應璩以諷諫。

translations.literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Du Xi composed ten poems, using the voice of Ying Qu to offer indirect admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Du Xi wrote ten poems in the voice of Ying Qu to offer veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 壽報曰：「省詩知意。

translations.literal: Shou replied, "Having read the poems I know the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied, "I have read the poems and understand your meaning.

sentences.zh: 若今人所作，乃賢哲之話言；

translations.literal: If they were written by men of today, they would be the instructive words of worthies and sages;
translations.idiomatic: If a living man wrote them, they would be the words of sages;

sentences.zh: 若古人所作，則死鬼之常辭耳。」

translations.literal: if written by men of old, they would be the commonplace phrases of dead ghosts, nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: if they came from the ancients, they would be nothing but the stale phrases of dead men."

sentences.zh: 燕王皝自以稱王未受晉命，冬，遣長史劉翔、參軍鞠運來獻捷論功，且言權假之間，並請刻期大舉，共平中原。

translations.literal: Yan King Murong Huang, considering that he had proclaimed himself king without receiving Jin's commission, in winter sent Chief Clerk Liu Xiang and Aide Counselor Ju Yun to present a report of victory and merit, and moreover to speak of the interval of provisional authority, jointly requesting a set date for a great undertaking to together pacify the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang of Yan, having proclaimed himself king without Jin's sanction, sent Chief Clerk Liu Xiang and Aide Ju Yun in winter to report victories and claim merit, explain his provisional rule, and ask for a fixed date to join Jin in reconquering the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 皝擊高句麗，兵及新城，高句麗王釗乞盟，乃還。

translations.literal: Huang attacked Goguryeo; the army reached Xincheng; the King of Goguryeo Ju begged for alliance and Huang then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang attacked Goguryeo and advanced as far as Xincheng. The Goguryeo king Ju sued for peace, and Huang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又使其子恪、霸擊宇文別部。

translations.literal: He also sent his sons Ke and Ba to attack a separate division of the Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his sons Ke and Ba against a Yuwen splinter tribe.

sentences.zh: 霸年十三，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: Ba was thirteen years old and in courage topped the Three Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was only thirteen, yet in bravery he outshone the entire army.

sentences.zh: 張駿立辟雍、明堂以行禮。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun established the Imperial Academy and Bright Hall to perform the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun built the Imperial Academy and Bright Hall and performed the ceremonial rites there.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以世子重華行涼州事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Heir Apparent Chonghua was put in charge of Liang Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Heir Apparent Chonghua was placed in charge of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁丑，趙太保桃豹卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, Zhao Grand Mentor Tao Bao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingchou, Grand Mentor Tao Bao of Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以驃騎將軍琅邪王岳為侍中、司徒。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Prince of Langye Yue was made Palace Attendant and Excellency over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Prince Yue of Langye was appointed Palace Attendant and Excellency over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 漢李弈寇巴東，守將勞楊敗死。

translations.literal: Li Yi of Han raided Badong; the defending general Lao Yang was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi of Han raided Badong; the defending commander Lao Yang was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚子朔，都亭文康侯庾亮薨。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on gengzi the new year's day, Yu Liang, Marquis Wen Kang of Duting, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengzi—the New Year's day—Yu Liang, Marquis Wen Kang of Duting, died.

sentences.zh: 以護軍將軍、錄尚書何充為中書令。

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing He Chong was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, General Who Protects the Army and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 庾戌，以南郡太守庾翼為都督江、荊、司、雍、梁、益六州諸軍事、安西將軍、荊州刺史，假節，代亮鎮武昌。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Yu Yi, Prefect of Nan Commandery, was made area commander over military affairs of the six provinces Jiang, Jing, Si, Yong, Liang, and Yi, General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Jing Province, with credential staff, replacing Liang at garrison in Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Yu Yi, Prefect of Nan Commandery, was made area commander over Jiang, Jing, Si, Yong, Liang, and Yi, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Jing Province, with full authority, succeeding Liang at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時人疑翼年少，不能繼其兄。

translations.literal: People of the time doubted that Yi was young and could not succeed his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Many wondered whether the younger Yi, still young, could fill his brother's place.

sentences.zh: 翼悉心為治，戎政嚴明，數年之間，公私充實，人皆稱其才。

translations.literal: Yi devoted himself wholeheartedly to governance; military and civil affairs were strict and clear; within a few years public and private stores were full, and everyone praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi threw himself into governing the province. Military and civil administration grew strict and efficient, and within a few years both the treasury and the people prospered. All agreed he had real ability.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以左光祿大夫陸玩為侍中、司空。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Left Grand Master of Splendor Lu Wan was made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Lu Wan, Left Grand Master of Splendor, was appointed Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 宇文逸豆歸忌慕容翰才名。

translations.literal: Yuwen Yidougui resented Murong Han's talent and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Yidougui grew jealous of Murong Han's ability and reputation.

sentences.zh: 翰乃陽狂酣飲，或臥自便利，或被發歌呼，拜跪乞食。

translations.literal: Han then feigned madness, drinking heavily; sometimes lying down to relieve himself, sometimes letting his hair loose to sing and shout, bowing and kneeling to beg for food.
translations.idiomatic: Han pretended to be mad. He drank without restraint, lay down to relieve himself in public, let his hair hang loose while singing and shouting, and bowed and begged for food.

sentences.zh: 宇文舉國賤之，不復省錄，以故得行來自遂，山川形便，皆默記之。

translations.literal: The whole Yuwen state despised him and no longer kept watch over him; thus he could come and go freely and silently memorized all the strategic features of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen looked down on him and stopped keeping track of him. He was free to travel as he pleased and quietly memorized every defile, pass, and river crossing.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝以翰初非叛亂，以猜嫌出奔，雖在它國，常潛為燕計；

translations.literal: King Murong Huang of Yan knew Han had not originally rebelled but fled because of suspicion; though in another state, he constantly worked secretly for Yan's benefit;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang of Yan knew Han had never truly rebelled but had fled under suspicion. Even in exile he still worked secretly for Yan;

sentences.zh: 乃遣商人王車通市於宇文部以窺翰。

translations.literal: He sent the merchant Wang Che to trade with the Yuwen tribe in order to observe Han.
translations.idiomatic: so he sent the merchant Wang Che to trade in Yuwen territory and find out how Han was faring.

sentences.zh: 翰見車，無言，撫膺頷之而已。

translations.literal: When Han saw Che, he said nothing but clutched his chest and nodded.
translations.idiomatic: When Han saw Che, he said nothing, only clutched his chest and nodded.

sentences.zh: 皝曰：「翰欲來也。」

translations.literal: Huang said, "Han wishes to come.
translations.idiomatic: Huang said, "Han wants to return.

sentences.zh: 復使車迎之。

translations.literal: He again sent Che to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Che again to bring him home.

sentences.zh: 翰彎弓三石餘，矢尤長大，皝為之造可手弓矢，使畫埋於道旁而密告之。

translations.literal: Han could draw a bow of more than three dan; his arrows were especially long and large. Huang had a bow and arrows made to fit his hand, had someone bury them by the roadside and secretly inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Han could draw a bow of more than three dan, and his arrows were unusually long. Huang had a bow and arrows made to a manageable weight, buried them beside the road, and secretly told him where they were.

sentences.zh: 二月，翰竊逸豆歸名馬，攜其二子過取弓矢，逃歸。

translations.literal: In the second month, Han stole Yidougui's famous horses, took his two sons, stopped to retrieve the bow and arrows, and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Han stole Yidougui's best horses, took his two sons along, picked up the buried bow and arrows on the way, and fled back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸使驍騎百餘追之。

translations.literal: Yidougui sent more than a hundred elite horsemen in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui sent more than a hundred picked horsemen after him.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「吾久客思歸，既得上馬，無復還理。

translations.literal: Han said, "I have long been a guest yearning to return; now that I am mounted, there is no turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Han called out, "I have longed to go home for years. Now that I am mounted, I will not turn back.

sentences.zh: 吾向日陽愚以誑汝，吾之故藝猶在，無為相逼，自取死了！」

translations.literal: I feigned folly before to deceive you; my old skills are still with me. Do not press me and bring death on yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: I played the fool before to deceive you, but my old skills are still with me. Do not press me and throw your lives away!

sentences.zh: 追騎輕之，直突而前。

translations.literal: The pursuers underestimated him and charged straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers took him lightly and charged straight at him.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「吾居汝國久恨恨，不欲殺汝；

translations.literal: Han said, "I have long lived in resentment in your state and do not wish to kill you;
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "I have lived in your land for years with old grievances, yet I do not wish to kill you;

sentences.zh: 汝去我百步立汝刀，吾射之，一發中者汝可還，不中者可來前。」

translations.literal: go a hundred paces from me and stand your blade upright; I will shoot at it—if one shot hits, you may return; if it misses, you may come forward.
translations.idiomatic: go a hundred paces off and stand your blade upright. I will shoot once. If I hit it, turn back. If I miss, you may come on.

sentences.zh: 追騎解刀立之，一發，正中其環，追騎散走。

translations.literal: The pursuers unsheathed their blades and stood them up; with one shot he hit the ring on the hilt exactly, and the pursuers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers drew their blades and planted them upright. With one shot Han struck the ring on the hilt squarely, and they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 皝聞翰至，大喜，恩遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Huang heard Han had arrived and was greatly delighted, treating him with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang learned Han had arrived, he was overjoyed and treated him with extraordinary favor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，有星孛於太微。

translations.literal: On gengchen, a broom star appeared in the Supreme Palace constellation.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, a broom star appeared in the Supreme Palace constellation.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁卯，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao, there was a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 漢人攻拔丹川，守將孟彥、劉齊、李秋皆死。

translations.literal: Han troops captured and took Danchuan; the defending generals Meng Yan, Liu Qi, and Li Qiu all died.
translations.idiomatic: Han forces took Danchuan by storm. The defending generals Meng Yan, Liu Qi, and Li Qiu were all killed.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍始都雲中之盛樂宮。

translations.literal: Prince Tuoba Shiyijian of Dai first established his capital at Shengle Palace in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Shiyijian, Prince of Dai, first made Shengle Palace in Yunzhong his capital.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎遺漢主壽書，欲與之連兵入寇，約中分江南。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao sent a letter to Han ruler Li Shou, wishing to join forces for an invasion and proposing to divide Jiangnan between them.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao wrote to Li Shou of Han proposing a joint invasion and an even split of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 壽大喜，遣散騎常侍王嘏、中常侍王廣使於趙；

translations.literal: Shou was greatly pleased and sent Regular Attendant of the Dispersal Cavalry Wang Gu and Palace Attendant Wang Guang as envoys to Zhao;
translations.idiomatic: Shou was delighted and sent Regular Attendant of the Dispersal Cavalry Wang Gu and Palace Attendant Wang Guang as envoys to Zhao;

sentences.zh: 龔壯諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang remonstrated, but Shou would not listen.

sentences.zh: 壽大修船艦，繕兵聚糧。

translations.literal: Shou greatly expanded his fleet, drilled troops and gathered grain.
translations.idiomatic: Shou greatly expanded his fleet, drilled troops, and stockpiled grain.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，以尚書令馬當為六軍都督，徵集士卒七萬餘人為舟師，大閱於成都，鼓噪盈江；

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, Director of the Masters of Writing Ma Dang was made commander of the Six Armies; more than seventy thousand troops were gathered as a river fleet and reviewed on a grand scale at Chengdu, with drums and shouts filling the river;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, Ma Dang, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made commander of the Six Armies. More than seventy thousand men were assembled as a river force and reviewed at Chengdu, drums and war cries filling the river;

sentences.zh: 壽登城觀之，有吞噬江南之志。

translations.literal: Shou ascended the wall to watch, with ambition to swallow Jiangnan whole.
translations.idiomatic: Shou climbed the city wall to watch and nursed the ambition of swallowing Jiangnan whole.

sentences.zh: 解思明諫曰：「我國小兵弱，吳、會險遠，圖之未易。」

translations.literal: Xie Siming remonstrated, saying, "Our state is small and our army weak; Wu and Hui are perilous and far—conquering them will not be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Siming remonstrated, "Our state is small and our army weak. Wu and Kuaiji are rugged and far away. They will not be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 壽乃命群臣大議利害。

translations.literal: Shou then ordered the ministers to debate the pros and cons at length.
translations.idiomatic: Shou then ordered the court to debate the matter at length.

sentences.zh: 龔壯曰：「陛下與胡通，孰若與晉通？

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang said, "Your Majesty, is it better to align with the barbarians or with Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang said, "Your Majesty, is it better to deal with the barbarians or with Jin?

sentences.zh: 胡，豺狼也，既滅晉，不得不北面事之；

translations.literal: The barbarians are wolves; once Jin is destroyed, you will have no choice but to serve them as your northern overlord;
translations.idiomatic: They are wolves. Once Jin is gone, you will have no choice but to bow north and serve them;

sentences.zh: 若與之爭天下，則強弱不敵，危亡之勢也，虞、虢之事，已然之戒，願陛下熟慮之。」

translations.literal: if you contend with them for the realm, strength and weakness will not match—it is a situation of peril and ruin. The affair of Yu and Guo is a warning already fulfilled; I urge Your Majesty to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: and if you then try to contend with them for the realm, you will be outmatched—a path to ruin. The tale of Yu and Guo is a warning already written. I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆以壯言為然，叩頭泣諫，壽乃止。

translations.literal: All the ministers approved Gong Zhuang's words, kowtowing and weeping in remonstrance, and Shou then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all agreed with Gong Zhuang, kowtowing and weeping in remonstrance, and Shou abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 士卒咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The soldiers all cried "Long live [the Emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers all shouted "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 龔壯以為人之行莫大於忠孝；

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang held that among human conduct nothing is greater than loyalty and filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang held that nothing in human conduct surpassed loyalty and filial piety;

sentences.zh: 既報父、叔之仇，又欲使壽事晉，壽不從。

translations.literal: having avenged his father and uncles, he also wished Shou to serve Jin; Shou would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: and having avenged his father and uncles, he now wanted Shou to submit to Jin. Shou refused.

sentences.zh: 乃詐稱耳聾，手不制物，辭歸，以文籍自娛，終身不復至成都。

translations.literal: He then feigned deafness and inability to control his hands, asked leave to return home, amused himself with books, and never came to Chengdu again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He then pretended to be deaf and unable to control his hands, asked leave to go home, amused himself with books, and never set foot in Chengdu again.

sentences.zh: 趙尚書令夔安卒。

translations.literal: Kui An, Director of the Masters of Writing of Zhao, died.
translations.idiomatic: Kui An, Director of the Masters of Writing in Zhao, died.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎命司、冀、青、徐、幽、并、雍七州之民五丁取三，四丁取二，合鄴城舊兵，滿五十萬，具船萬艘，自河通海，運谷千一百萬斛於樂安城。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao ordered that among the people of the seven provinces Si, Ji, Qing, Xu, You, Bing, and Yong, from every five men three were taken and from every four two were taken; together with the old troops at Ye city the force was brought to five hundred thousand; ten thousand ships were prepared; from the river routes to the sea, eleven million hu of grain were transported to Le'an city.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao conscripted men from the seven provinces of Si, Ji, Qing, Xu, You, Bing, and Yong—three from every five households, two from every four—until, together with the old troops at Ye, he had five hundred thousand men. He prepared ten thousand ships and moved eleven million hu of grain by river and sea to Le'an.

sentences.zh: 徙遼西、北平、漁陽萬餘戶於兗、豫、雍、洛四川之地。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand households from Liaoxi, Beiping, and Yuyang were relocated to the four provinces of Yan, Yu, Yong, and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand households from Liaoxi, Beiping, and Yuyang were moved to Yan, Yu, Yong, and Luo.

sentences.zh: 自幽州以東至白狼，大興屯田。

translations.literal: From You Province eastward to Bailang, military colonies were greatly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: From You Province east to Bailang he greatly expanded military farming colonies.

sentences.zh: 悉括取民馬，有敢私匿者腰斬，凡得四萬餘匹。

translations.literal: All horses among the people were requisitioned; anyone who dared hide them privately was cut in two at the waist; in all more than forty thousand mounts were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Every horse among the people was seized; anyone who hid one was cut in two at the waist. In all he obtained more than forty thousand mounts.

sentences.zh: 大閱於宛陽，欲以擊燕。

translations.literal: A grand review was held at Wanyang, with intent to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He held a grand review at Wanyang, intending to strike Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝謂諸將曰：「石虎自以樂安城防守重複，薊城南北必不設備，今若詭路出其不意，可盡破也。」

translations.literal: King Murong Huang of Yan told his generals, "Shi Hu, counting on redundant defenses at Le'an city, will surely leave Ji undefended north and south. If we now take a deceptive route and strike by surprise, we can destroy them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang of Yan told his generals, "Shi Hu trusts the layered defenses at Le'an and will surely leave Ji unguarded to north and south. If we take a hidden route and strike where he does not expect us, we can destroy him completely.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，皝帥諸軍入自蠮螉塞襲趙，戍將當道者皆禽之，直抵薊城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Huang led the armies in through the Mantis Pass to raid Zhao; garrison commanders blocking the way were all captured, and they reached Ji directly.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Huang led his armies in through Mantis Pass to raid Zhao. Every garrison commander in their path was captured, and they went straight to Ji.

sentences.zh: 趙幽州刺史石光擁兵數萬，閉城不敢出。

translations.literal: Shi Guang, Inspector of You Province of Zhao, had troops numbering in the tens of thousands but closed the city and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Guang, Zhao's Inspector of You, had tens of thousands of men but shut the gates and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 燕兵進破武遂津，入高陽，所至焚燒積聚，略三萬餘家而去。

translations.literal: Yan troops advanced, broke through Wusui Ford, entered Gaoyang, burned stores wherever they went, carried off more than thirty thousand households, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army broke through Wusui Ford, entered Gaoyang, burned stores wherever they went, carried off more than thirty thousand households, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 石光坐懦弱征還。

translations.literal: Shi Guang was recalled on account of cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Guang was recalled to court for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎以秦公韜為太尉，與太子宣迭日省可尚書奏事，專決賞刑，不復啟白。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao made Duke of Qin Shi Tao Grand Commander and, alternating days with Crown Prince Xuan, reviewed and approved memorials to the Masters of Writing, deciding rewards and punishments on their own authority without reporting to Hu.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao made Duke of Qin Shi Tao Grand Commander and, on alternating days with Crown Prince Xuan, reviewed memorials to the Masters of Writing and decided rewards and punishments on their own, without reporting to Hu.

sentences.zh: 司徒申鐘諫曰：「賞刑者，人君之大柄，不可以假人。

translations.literal: Excellency over the Masses Shen Zhong remonstrated, saying, "Rewards and punishments are the great handles of the ruler—they must not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Excellency over the Masses Shen Zhong remonstrated, "Rewards and punishments are the sovereign's greatest powers. They must not be handed to others.

sentences.zh: 所以防微杜漸，消逆亂於未然也。

translations.literal: By them one guards against the subtle and stops the gradual, extinguishing rebellion before it arises.
translations.idiomatic: They exist to check small wrongs before they grow and to crush rebellion before it starts.

sentences.zh: 太子職在視膳，不當豫政；

translations.literal: The crown prince's duty is to attend to the ruler's meals—he should not participate in government;
translations.idiomatic: A crown prince's duty is to attend his father's meals, not to meddle in government;

sentences.zh: 庶人邃以豫政致敗，覆車未遠也。

translations.literal: the commoner Sui met ruin through participating in government; the overturned cart is not far behind.
translations.idiomatic: the commoner Sui was ruined because he took part in government—the overturned cart is still before our eyes.

sentences.zh: 且二政分權，鮮不階禍。

translations.literal: Moreover, when two powers divide authority, few escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: And when two powers share authority, few escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 愛之不以道，適所以害之也。」

translations.literal: Loving someone without proper principle is precisely how one harms him.
translations.idiomatic: To love a son without proper restraint is precisely how one destroys him.

sentences.zh: 虎不聽。

translations.literal: Hu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 中謁者令申扁以慧悟辯給有寵於虎，宣亦暱之，使典機密。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Shen Bian, for his cleverness and eloquence, had Hu's favor; Xuan also grew close to him and put him in charge of confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Shen Bian won Hu's favor through quick wit and fluent speech. Xuan also grew close to him and put him in charge of confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 虎既不省事，而宣、韜皆好酣飲、畋獵；

translations.literal: Hu no longer attended to affairs himself, and both Xuan and Tao loved heavy drinking and hunting;
translations.idiomatic: Hu no longer attended to business himself, and both Xuan and Tao loved heavy drinking and hunting;

sentences.zh: 由是除拜、生殺皆決於扁，自九卿已下率皆望塵而拜。

translations.literal: hence appointments, promotions, life and death all were decided by Bian; from the Nine Ministers down, all largely bowed at the sight of his dust.
translations.idiomatic: so appointments, promotions, and executions all fell to Bian. From the Nine Ministers down, men bowed at the mere sight of his dust.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事孫珍病目，求方於侍中崔約，約戲之曰：「溺中則愈」。

translations.literal: Sun Zhen, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, had sick eyes and sought a prescription from Palace Attendant Cui Yue; Yue joked with him, saying, "Drowning in urine will cure it."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhen, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, had an eye ailment and asked Palace Attendant Cui Yue for a remedy. Yue joked, "Drown them in urine and they'll heal."

sentences.zh: 珍曰：「目何可溺？」

translations.literal: Zhen said, "How can eyes be drowned?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "How can eyes be drowned?

sentences.zh: 約曰：「卿目睕睕，正耐溺中。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "Your eyes are so bright and round—they can perfectly endure being drowned in urine.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Your eyes are so round and bright—they can perfectly stand being drowned in urine.

sentences.zh: 珍恨之，以白宣。

translations.literal: Zhen hated this and reported it to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen took offense and told Xuan.

sentences.zh: 宣于兄弟中最胡狀，目深，聞之怒，誅約父子。

translations.literal: Among the brothers Xuan most resembled the Hu in appearance, with deep-set eyes; hearing this he was enraged and executed Cui Yue and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Among the brothers Xuan looked most like a Hu tribesman, with deep-set eyes. Enraged at the insult, he executed Cui Yue and his son.

sentences.zh: 於是公卿以下畏珍側目。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the dukes and ministers down all feared Zhen and watched him with sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, everyone from the highest ministers down feared Zhen and watched him with sidelong glances.

sentences.zh: 燕公斌督邊州，亦好畋獵，常懸管而入。

translations.literal: Duke of Yan Bin supervised the border provinces and also loved hunting, often entering with suspended pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yan Bin supervised the frontier provinces and also loved the chase, often entering the hunt with pipes suspended from him.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍張賀度每裁諫之，斌怒，辱賀度。

translations.literal: Pacification-of-the-North General Zhang Hedou often restrained and remonstrated with him; Bin was angry and humiliated Hedou.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification-of-the-North General Zhang Hedou often checked and remonstrated with him. Bin grew angry and humiliated Hedou.

sentences.zh: 虎聞之，使主書禮儀持節監之。

translations.literal: Hu heard of this and sent Director of Documentation Li Yi with credential staff to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu heard of it, he sent Director of Documentation Li Yi with credential staff to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 斌殺儀，又欲殺賀度，賀度嚴衛馳白之。

translations.literal: Bin killed Yi and also wished to kill Hedou; Hedou tightened his guard and rode in haste to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Bin killed Yi and then tried to kill Hedou as well. Hedou tightened his guard and rode posthaste to report it.

sentences.zh: 虎遣尚書張離帥騎追斌，鞭之三百，免官歸第，誅其親信十餘人。

translations.literal: Hu sent Master of Writing Zhang Li leading cavalry in pursuit of Bin, had him flogged three hundred strokes, removed him from office and sent him home, and executed more than ten of his close followers.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Master of Writing Zhang Li with cavalry after Bin, had him flogged three hundred strokes, stripped him of office and sent him home, and executed more than ten of his intimates.

sentences.zh: 張駿遣別駕馬詵入貢於趙，表辭蹇傲；

translations.literal: Zhang Jun sent Assistant Administrator Ma Shen to bring tribute to Zhao; the memorial's language was haughty and insolent;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sent Assistant Administrator Ma Shen to Zhao with tribute, but the memorial he bore was haughty and insolent;

sentences.zh: 趙王虎怒，欲斬詵。

translations.literal: King Shi Hu of Zhao was angry and wished to execute Shen.
translations.idiomatic: King Shi Hu of Zhao was furious and wanted Shen executed.

sentences.zh: 侍中石璞諫曰：「今國家所當先除者，遺晉也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Shi Pu remonstrated, saying, "What the state ought to eliminate first is the remnant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shi Pu remonstrated, "What the state must destroy first is the remnant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 河西僻陋，不足為意。

translations.literal: Hexi is remote and crude—not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi is remote and insignificant—not worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 今斬馬詵，必征張竣，則兵力分而為二，建康復延數年之命矣。」

translations.literal: If Ma Shen is executed now, Zhang Jun will surely be attacked; then military strength will be divided in two and Jiankang will gain several more years of life.
translations.idiomatic: If you kill Ma Shen now, you will have to march against Zhang Jun. Our strength will be split in two, and Jiankang will gain years of life.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Hu abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 璞，苞之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Pu was the great-grandson of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu was the great-grandson of Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 初，漢將李閎為晉所獲，逃奔於趙，漢主壽致書於趙王虎以請之，署曰「趙王石君」。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han general Li Hong had been captured by Jin and fled to Zhao; Han ruler Li Shou wrote to King Shi Hu of Zhao to request his return, signing it "Lord Stone of Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Han general Li Hong had been captured by Jin and fled to Zhao. Li Shou of Han wrote to King Shi Hu of Zhao asking for his return, signing the letter "Lord Stone of Zhao."

sentences.zh: 虎不悅，付外議之。

translations.literal: Hu was displeased and referred the matter to outside deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was displeased and referred the matter to the outer court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 中書監王波曰：「今李閎以死自誓曰：『苟得歸骨於蜀，當糾帥宗族，混同王化。』

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Bo said, "Now Li Hong has sworn on his life, saying, 'If I can return my bones to Shu, I shall gather my clan and unify them under the king's transforming rule.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Bo said, "Li Hong has sworn on his life that if he can return his bones to Shu, he will rally his clan and bring them under the king's civilizing rule.

sentences.zh: 若其信也，則不煩一旅，坐定梁、益；

translations.literal: If he is sincere, then it would not require a single brigade to settle Liang and Yi by sitting still;
translations.idiomatic: If he means it, Liang and Yi can be settled without sending a single brigade;

sentences.zh: 若有前卻，不過失一亡命之人，於趙何損！

translations.literal: if he hesitates or retreats, it is only the loss of one fugitive—what harm to Zhao!
translations.idiomatic: and if he falters, Zhao loses only one fugitive. What harm is there in that?

sentences.zh: 李壽既僭大號，今以制詔與之，彼必酬返，不若復為書與之。」

translations.literal: Li Shou has already usurped the imperial title; if an imperial edict is now given him, he will surely respond in kind—it would be better to write him another letter instead.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou has already usurped an imperial title. If we send him an imperial edict now, he will answer in kind. Better to write him another letter instead.

sentences.zh: 會挹婁國獻楛矢石砮於趙，波因請以遺漢，曰：「使其知我能服遠方也。」

translations.literal: Just then the state of Yilou presented oak arrows and stone arrowheads to Zhao; Bo therefore requested that they be sent on to Han, saying, "Let them know that we can make the far regions submit.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yilou sent oak arrows and stone arrowheads to Zhao. Bo asked that they be forwarded to Han, saying, "Let them see that we can bring distant lands to heel.

sentences.zh: 虎從之，遣李閎歸，厚為之禮。

translations.literal: Hu agreed, sent Li Hong back, and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Hu agreed, sent Li Hong home, and treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 閎至成都，壽下詔曰：「羯使來庭，貢其楛矢。」

translations.literal: When Hong reached Chengdu, Shou issued an edict saying, "The Jie envoy came to court, offering their oak arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong reached Chengdu, Shou issued an edict: "The Jie envoy came to court and presented oak arrows in tribute.

sentences.zh: 虎聞之，怒，黜王波，以白衣領職。

translations.literal: Hu heard of this, was angry, demoted Wang Bo, and had him serve in office as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu heard of it, he was furious. He demoted Wang Bo and made him serve in office without rank.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕王皝使唐國內史陽裕等築城於柳城之北、龍山之西，立宗廟、宮闕，命曰龍城。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, King Murong Huang of Yan sent Interior Secretary of Tang Commandery Yang Yu and others to build a city north of Liucheng and west of Long Mountain, establishing ancestral temples and palace halls, and named it Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Murong Huang of Yan sent Yang Yu, Interior Secretary of Tang Commandery, and others to build a city north of Liucheng and west of Long Mountain. They erected ancestral temples and palace halls and named the place Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiazi the new year's day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiazi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 劉翔至建康，帝引見，問慕容鎮軍平安。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang reached Jiankang; the emperor received him in audience and asked whether Area Commander Murong was safe and well.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiang reached Jiankang, the emperor received him in audience and asked after the health of Murong, the area commander.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣受遣之日，朝服拜章。」

translations.literal: He replied, "On the day I was dispatched, I wore court dress and presented my memorial."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "On the day I was dispatched, I wore court dress and presented my memorial."

sentences.zh: 翔為燕王皝求大將軍、燕五章璽。

translations.literal: Xiang requested on behalf of King Murong Huang of Yan the title Grand General and the five seals of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang asked on Murong Huang's behalf for the title Grand General and the five seals of Yan.

sentences.zh: 朝議以為；

translations.literal: The court deliberation held that;
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberation held that;

sentences.zh: 「故事：大將軍不處邊；

translations.literal: "By precedent: the Grand General does not hold a frontier post;
translations.idiomatic: "By precedent, the Grand General does not hold a frontier command;

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏以來，不封異姓為王。

translations.literal: since Han and Wei, no surname other than the imperial one has been enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: and since Han and Wei no one outside the imperial surname has been enfeoffed as king.

sentences.zh: 所求不可許。」

translations.literal: The request cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: These requests cannot be granted.

sentences.zh: 翔曰：「自劉、石構亂，長江以北，剪為戎藪，未聞中華公卿之冑有一人能攘臂揮戈、摧破凶逆者也。

translations.literal: Xiang said, "Since Liu and Shi stirred up chaos, north of the Yangtze River has been cut away into a barbarian den. One has not heard of a single person among the descendants of Chinese public ministers and officials who could roll up his sleeves, wave a spear, and smash the vicious rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang replied, "Since Liu Yuan and Shi Le plunged the realm into chaos, everything north of the Yangtze has become barbarian territory. Not one descendant of the Chinese nobility has been heard to roll up his sleeves, take up arms, and break the power of these ruthless rebels.

sentences.zh: 獨慕容鎮軍父子竭力，心存本朝，以寡擊眾，屢殄強敵，使石虎畏懼，悉徙邊陲之民散居三魏，蹙國千里，以薊城為北境。

translations.literal: Only Area Commander Murong and his sons exerted themselves to the utmost; their hearts preserved loyalty to the dynasty. With the few they struck the many, repeatedly exterminated powerful enemies, made Shi Hu fear, wholly moved the people of the border regions to scatter and dwell in the Three Wei, compressed the state by a thousand li, and made Ji City the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Only Murong, the area commander, and his sons exerted themselves loyally on the court's behalf. Again and again they routed superior enemy forces with inferior numbers, until Shi Hu was frightened into moving all the frontier population into the Three Wei commanderies, shrinking his domain by a thousand li and making Ji his northern boundary.

sentences.zh: 功烈如此，而惜海北之地不以為封邑，何哉！

translations.literal: Merits and achievements such as these—yet one grudges the lands north of the sea and does not grant them as a fief. Why!
translations.idiomatic: With achievements like these, why grudge them the lands north of the sea as a fief?

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖不愛王爵於韓、彭，故能成其帝業；

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Gaozu of Han did not begrudge royal ranks to Han Xin and Peng Yue, and therefore was able to complete his imperial enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Gaozu of Han did not withhold kingship from Han Xin and Peng Yue, and so he was able to win the empire;

sentences.zh: 項羽刓印不忍授，卒用危亡。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu filed down the seals and could not bear to grant them, and in the end brought on peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu filed down the seal and could not bring himself to confer it, and in the end was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 吾之至心，非敬欲尊其所事，竊惜聖朝疏忠義之國，使四海無所勸慕耳。」

translations.literal: My utmost sincerity is not that I respect and wish to exalt the one he serves; I privately regret that the sage dynasty treats a loyal and righteous state with neglect, leaving the four seas with no one to encourage and emulate."
translations.idiomatic: I speak from the heart—not to honor Murong for his own sake, but because I fear the court is slighting a loyal ally, leaving the empire with no model to follow."

sentences.zh: 尚書諸葛恢，翔之姊夫也，獨主異議，以為：「夷狄相攻，中國之利。
