translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Zhuge Hui, Xiang's elder sister's husband, alone upheld the dissenting view, holding that: "When barbarians attack one another, it is to China's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Hui, Director of the Masters of Writing and Xiang's brother-in-law, was alone in dissenting. He argued, "When barbarians fight among themselves, China profits.

sentences.zh: 惟器與名，不可輕許。」

translations.literal: Only office and title must not be lightly granted."
translations.idiomatic: Rank and title must not be granted lightly."

sentences.zh: 乃謂翔曰：「借使慕容鎮軍能除石虎，乃是復得一石虎也，朝廷何賴焉！」

translations.literal: He then said to Xiang: "Even supposing Area Commander Murong could remove Shi Hu, this would only mean gaining another Shi Hu—upon what could the court rely!"
translations.idiomatic: He then told Xiang, "Even if Murong could destroy Shi Hu, you would simply get another Shi Hu. What good would that do the court?"

sentences.zh: 翔曰：「嫠婦猶知恤宗周之隕。

translations.literal: Xiang said, "Even a widow knows to care for the fall of the ancestral Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Even a widow knows to grieve for the fall of the Zhou house.

sentences.zh: 今晉室阽危，君位侔元、豈，曾無憂國之心邪？

translations.literal: Now the Jin house stands on the brink of peril; your rank equals Yuan and Qi—have you truly no heart to worry for the state?
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house now teeters on the brink, yet you hold rank to match Du Yu and Pei Kai—do you have no care for the realm?

sentences.zh: 向使靡、鬲之功不立，則少康何以祀夏！

translations.literal: If in former times the achievements of Mi and Ge had not been established, then how could Shaokang have sacrificed to Xia!
translations.idiomatic: Had Mi and Ge not done their work, how could Shaokang have restored the Xia!

sentences.zh: 桓、文之戰不捷，則同人皆為左衣任矣。

translations.literal: If the battles of Duke Huan and Duke Wen had not been victorious, then everyone within would have worn the left lapels of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Had Duke Huan and Duke Wen failed in their campaigns, all within the realm would wear barbarian dress with the left lapel folded.

sentences.zh: 慕容鎮軍枕戈待旦，志殄凶逆，而君更唱邪惑之言，忌間忠臣。

translations.literal: Area Commander Murong sleeps upon his spear awaiting the dawn, his will set on exterminating the vicious rebels—yet you instead raise perverse and deceiving words and sow jealousy between loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Murong sleeps with a spear at his pillow, ready at dawn to destroy these rebels—yet you spread perverse counsel and drive wedges between loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 四海所以未壹，良由君輩耳！」

translations.literal: The reason the four seas are not yet unified is truly because of you people!"
translations.idiomatic: It is men like you who are keeping the empire from reunification!"

sentences.zh: 翔留建康歲餘，眾議終不決。

translations.literal: Xiang remained at Jiankang for more than a year; the assembly's deliberations in the end were never decided.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang stayed at Jiankang for more than a year, but the court never reached a decision.

sentences.zh: 翔乃說中常侍彧弘曰：「石虎苞八州之地，帶甲百萬，志吞江、漢，自索頭、宇文暨諸小國，無不臣服；

translations.literal: Xiang then persuaded Palace Attendant Yu Hong, saying, "Shi Hu embraces the lands of eight provinces, bears a million armored troops, and intends to swallow the Yangtze and Han regions; from Suotou, Yuwen, and all the small states, none fail to submit;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then appealed to Palace Attendant Yu Hong: "Shi Hu holds eight provinces and commands a million armored men. He aims to swallow the Yangtze and Han basins. From the Tuoba and Yuwen down to every petty state, all submit to him;

sentences.zh: 惟慕容鎮軍翼戴天子，精貫白日，而更不獲禮之命，竊恐天下移心解體，無復南向者矣。

translations.literal: Only Area Commander Murong supports and upholds the Son of Heaven, his loyalty piercing through to the white sun—yet he still does not receive a grant of ritual honors. I privately fear that under heaven hearts will shift and the body politic dissolve, and there will no longer be those who turn southward.
translations.idiomatic: Only Murong supports the Son of Heaven with loyalty bright as the sun—yet the court still withholds its honors. I fear the realm will lose heart and fall apart, and none will look south toward Jin again.

sentences.zh: 公孫淵無尺寸之益於吳，吳主封為燕王，加以九錫。

translations.literal: Gongsun Yuan brought not the slightest benefit to Wu, yet the Lord of Wu enfeoffed him as King of Yan and added the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan did not advance Wu's interests in the least, yet the Wu emperor made him King of Yan and bestowed the Nine Honors.

sentences.zh: 今慕容鎮軍屢摧賊鋒，威振秦、隴，虎比遣重使，甘言厚幣，欲授以曜威大將軍、遼西王；

translations.literal: Now Area Commander Murong has repeatedly shattered the enemy's vanguard, his prestige shaking Qin and Long. Hu has lately sent important envoys with honeyed words and rich gifts, wishing to appoint him Grand General of Dazzling Might and King of Liaoxi;
translations.idiomatic: Murong has repeatedly broken the enemy's spearhead until his fame shakes Qin and Long. Shi Hu has just sent high envoys with sweet words and rich gifts, offering him Grand General of Dazzling Might and the kingship of Liaoxi;

sentences.zh: 慕容鎮軍惡其非正，卻而不受。

translations.literal: Area Commander Murong hated that it was not legitimate and refused it, not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Murong rejected the offer as illegitimate and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷乃矜惜虛名，沮抑忠順，豈社稷之長計乎！

translations.literal: Now the court grudges empty titles and suppresses the loyal and obedient—can this be the long-term plan for the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court grudges empty titles and thwarts a loyal ally—is that a policy fit for the state?

sentences.zh: 後雖悔之，恐無及己。」

translations.literal: Though one may regret it later, I fear it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Regret afterward may come too late."

sentences.zh: 弘為之入言於帝，帝意亦欲許之。

translations.literal: Hong entered on his behalf and spoke to the emperor; the emperor's mind also wished to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong conveyed this to the emperor, who also inclined to grant the request.

sentences.zh: 會皝上表稱：「庾氏兄弟擅權召亂，宜加斥退，以安社稷。」

translations.literal: Just then Huang submitted a memorial stating: "The Yu brothers monopolize power and summon chaos; they should be further repelled and dismissed, so as to settle the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Murong Huang submitted a memorial: "The Yu brothers have seized power and brought ruin upon the realm. They ought to be removed so the state may be secured."

sentences.zh: 又與庾冰書，責其當國秉權，不能為國雪恥。

translations.literal: He also wrote to Yu Bing, reproaching him for holding power while directing the state and being unable to wipe away the nation's disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Yu Bing, rebuking him for holding the reins of government yet failing to avenge the nation's humiliation.

sentences.zh: 冰甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，乃與何充奏從其請。

translations.literal: Bing was greatly afraid; because Murong was utterly distant and not someone he could control, he then together with He Chong memorialized to follow his request.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was terrified. Murong was too far away to control, so he and He Chong memorialized that the court should accede to the request.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以慕容皝為使持節、大將軍、都督河北諸軍事、幽州牧、大單于、燕王，備物、典策，皆從殊禮。

translations.literal: On yimao, Murong Huang was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Hebei, Governor of You Province, Grand Chanyu, and King of Yan; the ceremonial objects and investiture documents all followed exceptional ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Murong Huang was made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, commander of all Hebei forces, Governor of You, Grand Chanyu, and King of Yan, with full ceremonial honors accorded by special rite.

sentences.zh: 又以其世子俊為假節、安北將軍、東夷校尉、左賢王；

translations.literal: Further, his heir Jun was made Bearer of Provisional Staff, Pacifier of the North General, Commandant of the Eastern Yi, and Left Worthy King;
translations.idiomatic: His heir Jun was also appointed provisional staff bearer, Pacifier of the North, Commandant of the Eastern Yi, and Left Worthy King;

sentences.zh: 賜軍資器械以千萬計。

translations.literal: Military supplies and weapons were granted numbering in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Military supplies and weapons were granted by the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 又封諸功臣百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred meritorious officers were also enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred other meritorious men were also enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 以劉翔為代郡太守，封臨泉鄉侯，加員外散騎常侍；

translations.literal: Liu Xiang was appointed Administrator of Dai Commandery, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linquan Township, and added as Supernumerary Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang was made Administrator of Dai Commandery, enfeoffed as Marquis of Linquan Township, and given the added title Supernumerary Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates;

sentences.zh: 翔固辭不受。

translations.literal: Xiang firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang firmly declined them all.

sentences.zh: 翔疾江南士大夫以驕奢酣縱相尚，嘗因朝貴宴集，謂何充等曰：「四海板蕩，奄逾三紀，宗社為墟，黎民塗炭，斯乃廟堂焦慮之時，忠臣畢命之秋也。

translations.literal: Xiang loathed that the scholar-officials of Jiangnan took pride in extravagance and drunken indulgence as things to emulate; once at a gathering of court nobles, he said to He Chong and others: "The four seas are in upheaval, suddenly surpassing three reign-periods; the ancestral altars are ruins, the common people scorched and charred—this is precisely the time for the court hall to burn with anxiety, the season for loyal ministers to exhaust their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang detested the indulgent luxury of Jiangnan's gentry. At a banquet of court grandees he told He Chong and the others, "The realm has been in turmoil for three full generations. The altars lie in ruins and the people in ashes. This is the hour for the throne to burn with worry and for loyal ministers to give their lives.

sentences.zh: 而諸君宴安江沱，肆情縱欲，以奢靡為榮，以傲誕為賢；

translations.literal: Yet you gentlemen feast at ease on the Jiang's bends, give rein to passion and indulgence, take extravagant display as glory, and take arrogant extravagance as worthiness;
translations.idiomatic: Yet you feast in comfort on the Yangtze, indulge every appetite, take extravagance for distinction, and call insolent excess virtue;

sentences.zh: 謇諤之言不聞，征伐之功不立，將何以尊主濟民乎！」

translations.literal: Straightforward and reproving words are not heard; the achievements of campaigns are not established—how will you exalt the lord and succor the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Straight counsel goes unheeded and no conquests are won—how then will you serve your sovereign and save the people?"

sentences.zh: 充等甚慚。

translations.literal: Chong and the others were deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the others were deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 詔遣兼大鴻臚郭烯持節詣棘城冊命燕王，與翔等偕北。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Guo Xi, bearing staff credentials, to proceed to Jicheng to invest the King of Yan, going north together with Xiang and others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Guo Xi, Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies, bearing credentials to Jicheng to invest the King of Yan. He traveled north with Xiang and his party.

sentences.zh: 公卿餞於江上，翔謂諸公曰：「昔少康資一旅以滅有窮，勾踐憑會稽以報強吳；

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers saw them off on the riverbank; Xiang said to the assembled lords: "In the past Shaokang relied on a single brigade to destroy Youqiong; Goujian relied on Kuaiji to avenge himself upon mighty Wu;
translations.idiomatic: The court nobles saw them off on the river. Xiang told them, "Once Shaokang destroyed Youqiong with a single brigade, and Goujian on Mount Kuaiji avenged himself on mighty Wu;

sentences.zh: 蔓草猶宜早除，況寇仇乎！

translations.literal: Even creeping weeds should still be removed early—how much more so enemy foes!
translations.idiomatic: If creeping weeds must be uprooted early, how much more a sworn enemy!

sentences.zh: 今石虎、李壽，志相吞噬，王師縱未能澄清北方，且當從事巴、蜀。

translations.literal: Now Shi Hu and Li Shou intend to devour each other; even if the royal army cannot yet clarify and pacify the north, it ought at least to take action in Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu and Li Shou now hunger to devour each other. Even if the royal army cannot yet recover the north, it should at least move against Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 一旦石虎先入舉事，並壽而有之，據形便之地以臨東南，雖有智者，不能善其後矣。」

translations.literal: Once Shi Hu first rises in action, annexes Shou, and possesses both, holding a terrain-advantageous position to overlook the southeast—even if there were a wise man, he could not put things right afterward."
translations.idiomatic: If Shi Hu strikes first, overruns Li Shou, and holds the strategic lands overlooking the southeast, even the wisest adviser will not be able to remedy what follows."

sentences.zh: 中護軍謝廣曰：「是吾心也！」

translations.literal: Central Guard General Xie Guang said, "That is my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Central Guard General Xie Guang said, "That is exactly my mind!"

sentences.zh: 三月，戊戌，皇后杜氏崩。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuxu, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuxu, Empress Du died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁卯，葬恭皇后於興平陵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, Empress Gong was buried at Xingping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on dingmao, Empress Gong was buried at Xingping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 詔實王公以下至庶人皆正土斷、白籍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from kings and dukes down to common people all should rectify land registration and white registers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered princes, officials, and commoners alike to register land holdings and unregistered households.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，郭烯、劉翔等至燕，燕王皝以翔為東夷護軍、領大將軍長史，以唐國內史陽裕為左司馬，典書令李洪為右司馬，中尉鄭林為軍諮祭灑。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Guo Xi, Liu Xiang, and others reached Yan; King of Yan Huang appointed Xiang Eastern Yi Protector General and concurrently Grand General's Chief Clerk; Interior Secretary of Tang State Yang Yu as Left Major; Director of Documents Li Hong as Right Major; Commandant of the Guard Zheng Lin as Army Staff Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Guo Xi, Liu Xiang, and the rest reached Yan. King Murong Huang made Xiang Protector General of the Eastern Yi and chief clerk to the Grand General, appointed Yang Yu, Interior Secretary of Tang, as Left Major, Li Hong, Director of Documents, as Right Major, and Zheng Lin, Commandant of the Guard, as Army Staff Adviser.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛酉，東海哀王沖薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Lamented King Chong of Donghai died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Prince Chong of Donghai died.

sentences.zh: 九月，代王什翼犍築盛樂城於故城南八里。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Tuoba Shiyijian of Dai built Shengle City eight li south of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Tuoba Shiyijian, King of Dai, built Shengle City eight li south of the old capital.

sentences.zh: 代王妃慕容氏卒。

translations.literal: The princess consort of Dai of the Murong clan died.
translations.idiomatic: The Murong princess, consort to the King of Dai, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，匈奴劉虎寇代西部，代王什翼犍遣軍逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Xiongnu Liu Hu raided the western part of Dai; King Shiyijian of Dai sent troops to intercept and attack, crushing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Xiongnu chief Liu Hu raided western Dai. King Shiyijian sent troops against him and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 虎卒，子務桓立，遣使求和於代，什翼犍以女妻之。

translations.literal: Hu died; his son Wuhuan was established, sent envoys seeking peace with Dai, and Shiyijian gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu died. His son Wuhuan succeeded him and sent envoys seeking peace with Dai. Shiyijian gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 務桓又朝貢於趙，趙以務桓為平北將軍、左賢王。

translations.literal: Wuhuan also presented tribute at court to Zhao; Zhao appointed Wuhuan Pacifier of the North General and Left Worthy King.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuan also sent tribute to Zhao, which made him Pacifier of the North and Left Worthy King.

sentences.zh: 趙橫海將軍王華帥舟師自海道襲燕安平，破之。

translations.literal: Zhao's Crossing-the-Sea General Wang Hua led a fleet by sea route to raid Anping in Yan and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, Zhao's Crossing-the-Sea General, led a naval force by sea against Anping in Yan and took it.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝以慕容恪為渡遼將軍，鎮平郭。

translations.literal: King of Yan Huang appointed Murong Ke Crossing-the-Liao General and garrisoned Pingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang appointed Murong Ke Crossing-the-Liao General and stationed him at Pingguo.

sentences.zh: 自慕容翰、慕容仁之後，諸將無能繼者。

translations.literal: Since Murong Han and Murong Ren, among the generals there were none who could succeed them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Murong Han and Murong Ren, no general had been able to fill their place.

sentences.zh: 及恪至平郭，撫舊懷新，屢破高句麗兵，高句麗畏之，不敢入境。

translations.literal: When Ke reached Pingguo, he treated the old with kindness and embraced the new; repeatedly he broke Goguryeo troops; Goguryeo feared him and dared not cross the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke reached Pingguo, he won over old subjects and new alike, repeatedly routed Goguryeo armies, and so thoroughly intimidated them that they dared not cross the border.

sentences.zh: 十二月，興平康伯陸玩薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Kang Bo Lu Wan of Xingping died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Lu Wan, Viscount Kang of Xingping, died.

sentences.zh: 漢主壽以其太子勢領大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Han ruler Shou had his heir Shi lead as Grand General and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou of Han had his heir Li Shi serve as Grand General and overseer of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，成主雄以儉約寬惠得蜀人心。

translations.literal: Initially, ruler Xiong of Cheng won the hearts of Shu through frugality and generous kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Xiong of Cheng had won the loyalty of Shu through thrift and generous rule.

sentences.zh: 及李閎、王嘏還自鄴，盛稱鄴中繁庶，宮殿壯麗；

translations.literal: When Li Hong and Wang Gu returned from Ye, they lavishly praised Ye's prosperity and the splendor of its palaces;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hong and Wang Gu returned from Ye, they spoke endlessly of the city's wealth and the grandeur of its palaces;

sentences.zh: 且言趙王虎以刑殺御下，故能控制境內。

translations.literal: and added that King Shi Hu of Zhao ruled his subordinates through punishments and executions, and therefore could control his territory.
translations.idiomatic: and told how King Shi Hu ruled by terror, which was why he kept his realm under control.

sentences.zh: 壽慕之，徙旁郡民三丁以上者以實成都，大修宮室，治器玩；

translations.literal: Shou admired this, moved people from neighboring commanderies—all males of three ding and above—to fill Chengdu, greatly repaired palaces, and crafted ornamental objects;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou envied this. He moved every registered male of three ding or more from neighboring commanderies into Chengdu, greatly enlarged the palace, and piled up luxury goods;

sentences.zh: 人有小過，輒殺以立威。

translations.literal: If people had small faults, he immediately killed them to establish authority.
translations.idiomatic: For the slightest offense he executed men to terrify others.

sentences.zh: 左僕射蔡興、右僕射李嶷皆坐直諫死。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Cai Xing and Right Vice Director Li Yi both died because of their direct remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Cai Xing and Right Vice Director Li Yi were both executed for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 民疲於賦役，吁嗟滿道，思亂者眾矣。」」」

translations.literal: The people were exhausted by taxes and corvée; sighs and laments filled the roads; those who thought of rebellion were many.”
translations.idiomatic: The people were worn down by taxes and forced labor. Lament filled the roads, and many began to look toward revolt.”
